Most investors chase solar, electric vehicles and aluminium producers.

But the real opportunity may also lie in the critical materials that keep these industries running. 👀

🏭 RAIN INDUSTRIES deserves a closer look.

Here’s why two products — CPC (Calcined Petroleum Coke) and CTP (Coal Tar Pitch) — could become important drivers to watch.

🔹 Both play a crucial role in manufacturing carbon anodes used in aluminium smelting.

🔹 Aluminium demand is linked to power infrastructure, transportation, renewable energy and industrial growth.

🔹 If CPC and CTP prices rise, Rain Industries could benefit — depending on its selling prices, raw-material costs, volumes and margins.

📈 The key isn't just rising prices. It's whether higher prices translate into better profitability and cash flow.

⚠️ Investors should also track input costs, global aluminium demand, debt and working-capital requirements.

🎯 Sometimes, the interesting part of a megatrend lies deeper in the supply chain.

Is Rain Industries a potential beneficiary of the next carbon-materials upcycle? Worth watching — but the numbers must confirm the thesis.

Tata Technologies duniya ki car aur aerospace companies ke liye engineering ka kaam karti hai: nayi gaadi design karna, uska software, manufacturing ki planning. Tata Motors aur JLR iske bade customers rahe hain.

PLUS (+)
+ Revenue ₹1,699 cr, +28% YoY
+ Services ₹1,356 cr, +34% YoY
+ Dollar mein services +4.3% QoQ (constant currency)
+ EBITDA ₹273 cr, +32%, margin 16.1%
+ Ek luxury European car company se $138 mn ka full-vehicle program, saath mein kai aur deals

MINUS (−)
− EBIT ₹222 cr se ₹219 cr, margin 13.3% se 12.9%
− Net profit ₹171 cr: last year ₹166 cr, pichhli quarter ₹181 cr
− Total revenue QoQ sirf +2%
− CFO ne kuch customer segments aur geographies mein near-term challenges maane

Gap kahan se aaya?
EBITDA aur EBIT ke beech depreciation aur amortisation hoti hai. Yeh pichhli quarter lagbhag ₹45 cr thi, ab lagbhag ₹54 cr. Iske neeche byaaj, other income aur tax ne bhi profit ko rokka, lekin company ne inka breakdown nahi diya. 28% YoY growth mein ES-Tec acquisition ka hissa kitna hai, yeh bhi alag se nahi bataya gaya. Management ne pehle ES-Tec ko FY27 ka growth driver bataya tha.

Management ka kehna hai ki FY27 mein "strong double-digit growth" aayegi.

Kya khatakta hai?
Auto industry par bhaari nirbharta. Car companies jab naye model ya EV ka kharcha kaatti hain, to engineering services sabse pehle katti hain. Employees 12,895 hain aur attrition 15.6%.

Aage kya dekhein:
- $138 mn program kitni tezi se revenue banta hai
- EBIT margin 13% ke aas-paas tikta hai ya nahi
- Organic aur acquired growth ka farq
- Revenue QoQ fir tez hoti hai ya nahi

Important: A good business cycle does not automatically make a stock cheap. The share price, valuation, debt and sustainability of earnings still matter.

8/13 - The financial results are already showing improvement

Rain Industries' June 2026 quarter, as presented in the report:

Revenue:

₹5,167 crore, up 17% year on year.

EBITDA:

₹994 crore, up 61% year on year.

EBITDA margin:

Approximately 19.2%, compared with around 14% a year earlier.

Net profit:

₹341 crore, compared with ₹83 crore in June 2025.

The report also shows March 2026 revenue of ₹4,521 crore and net profit of ₹121 crore, versus a net loss of ₹138 crore in March 2025.

The key point is that EBITDA grew much faster than revenue, while margins expanded.

That is consistent with improving operating profitability.

2/13 - First, understand what Rain Industries does

Rain is not just a single-product company.

Its major businesses include:

→ Carbon: Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) and Coal Tar Pitch (CTP)

→ Advanced Materials: Speciality and high-value carbon-based materials

→ Cement: Cement manufacturing

The carbon business is central to this investment thesis because CPC and CTP are essential materials for aluminium production.

Rain Industries: The real opportunity is beyond the headline numbers.

Most investors look at solar panels, EVs and aluminium.

But very few understand the materials required to manufacture aluminium anodes.

Rain Industries operates in this important part of the industrial supply chain.

Here is why rising CPC and CTP prices could matter for the company. 🧵

Few Companies Q2 FY 27 Result Updates (which we are tracking)

1) Sejal Glass:
Sejal Glass’s Q2 consolidated PAT rose 78% YoY to ₹14.4cr and doubled from Q1’s ₹7.2cr. Revenue grew 33% to ₹138.1cr. No exceptional item, and other income is just ₹1.8cr. The number I’d read first isn’t in the headline.

The listed company’s own standalone books earned ₹0.67cr of PAT on ₹41.3cr of revenue. The foreign subsidiary, per the auditor’s note, earned ₹13.65cr on ₹97cr. That’s 70% of group revenue and about 95% of group profit, at a 14% net margin against 1.6% at the parent. For profit purposes, Sejal Glass the listed company is mostly Sejal Glass & Glass Manufacturing Products LLC.

The margin move is real. Operating margin hit 17.3%, the highest of the last ten quarters, against 13.7% in Q1 and 16.2% a year ago. Operating profit is ₹23.9cr vs ₹16.8cr.

Two things trim the headline. Shares are up 13%, so EPS grew 57% (₹12.52 vs ₹7.95), not 78%. And the subsidiary’s accounts were reviewed by a separate auditor, with the group auditor relying on that report.

On cash, H1 operating cash flow of ₹34.9cr covered ₹22.7cr of capex. Cash doubled to ₹23.3cr and borrowings are roughly flat, though ₹13cr of that operating cash came from higher payables. Receivables are ₹146cr, more than a full quarter’s revenue.

2) TARIL
TARIL’s Q2: consolidated PAT up 118% YoY to ₹81.4cr, EPS ₹2.66 vs ₹1.13. Revenue grew 60.7% to ₹739.4cr. PBT equals profit before exceptional items in this filing, and other income actually fell (₹13.9cr to ₹2.7cr), so none of this growth leans on anything but the core business.

A parent-company profit that goes up 4x is exactly the number I go and check before believing.

Here’s what held my attention. Standalone PAT went from ₹16.8cr to ₹75cr. Consolidated only doubled. That gap is the subsidiaries: group PAT minus parent PAT was about ₹20.6cr last year and just ₹6.4cr this year. The parent did all the lifting, with other expenses flat at ₹62.8cr (vs ₹65.8cr) on ₹281cr more revenue. That looks like real operating leverage.

The context that matters here is the base. Q2 last year was soft, with standalone PBT of ₹25.6cr against roughly ₹81cr in Q1 FY26. H1 is the fairer read, and standalone PBT is up 56% there. Still strong, just not 4x.

Now the forward part. The order book is ₹7,237cr, with Q2 inflow of ₹1,169cr (+97%), executable over 18–24 months. That needs roughly ₹3,600–4,800cr a year of revenue, and FY26 was ₹2,509cr. Borrowings are up ~₹117cr since March and capital WIP has nearly doubled, so the Changodar plant has to arrive on time. Commercial production is expected around Diwali.

Worth watching Q3, the first quarter Changodar can contribute. The new UK subsidiary, incorporated in September with no capital in it yet, is the other thing to track.

3) Accent Microcell
Accent Microcell’s H1 FY27: PAT up 72% YoY to ₹31.1cr, EPS ₹12.97 vs ₹7.84. Revenue grew 25.4% to ₹174.8cr. No exceptional item, other income flat at ₹2.6cr, tax rate unchanged near 25% — so none of this leans on anything but operations.

Profit growing nearly 3x as fast as revenue is the number I go and check.

PBT rose ₹17.3cr, and the segment note shows where. Dahej (export) added ₹11.9cr on 56% higher export revenue, with segment margin steady near 27%. Pirana added ₹6.5cr even though its domestic revenue fell 10% — segment profit went from ₹0.3cr to ₹6.8cr.

Also, check out the debtor days & working capital days and you will realise that demand is getting stronger & stronger.

What looks behind it: purchases of stock-in-trade dropped from ₹38cr to ₹3cr, and materials fell from 60% to 52% of revenue. Reads like the mix moving from trading to own manufacturing.

Forward-looking: capex was ₹61cr in six months, and capital WIP of ₹135cr is now 2.4x PP&E. The MCC plant was budgeted at ₹32cr in the rights issue and has absorbed ₹63cr, the balance from internal accruals, with no deviation reported. Debt is just ₹0.6cr, so this is being funded from cash flow and the two fundraises.

Worth watching how fast those plants start earning.

Sejal Glass is up ~20% today and this time there is a clear fundamental trigger behind the move.

Q2 FY27:
Revenue ₹138 Cr, +33% YoY Operating margin ~17.3% vs ~16.3% PAT ₹14.4 Cr, +78% YoY PAT nearly doubled sequentially from Q1

But the bigger story is what is changing underneath.

India’s flat-glass market is benefiting from premium housing, offices, airports, metros, data centres and the shift toward energy-efficient buildings.

And demand is increasingly moving away from plain glass toward insulated, laminated and other processed glass.

That is exactly where Sejal is positioning itself.

Its UAE order book had already increased to ~₹186 Cr, while 
India had secured ₹50 Cr+ of orders from customers including Godrej, L&T, Prestige and Raheja.

There are multiple company-specific triggers ahead.

The third UAE tempering line and fire-rated glass technology are targeted to start commercial production in Q3 FY27.

Capacity utilisation is also being ramped across Silvassa, Taloja, Erode and UAE, creating operating-leverage potential.

Railway glass is another emerging vertical, with Sejal already approved across major Indian Railways manufacturing facilities.

So the business is gradually moving from conventional architectural glass toward higher-value insulated, laminated, fire-rated, digital and railway glass.

Management is targeting 25-40% annual revenue growth over the next few years, with railway + fire-rated glass expected to become increasingly meaningful.

TARIL: Revenue up 61%. PAT up 117%. Order inflow up 97%.

But the most important part of Transformers & Rectifiers India’s Q2 FY27 results is what these numbers reveal about the business.

1. 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗚𝗥𝗢𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗔𝗡 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗨𝗘

Revenue grew 61% YoY to ₹739 Cr, while EBITDA rose 119% to ₹129 Cr.

EBITDA margin expanded from 12.8% to 17.4%.

This is operating leverage: as capacity utilisation improves, profits can grow faster than sales. The important question is whether these margins are sustainable.

2. 𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗘𝗥 𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗖𝗖𝗘𝗟𝗘𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚

Q2 order inflow: ₹1,169 Cr, up 97% YoY.

H1 order inflow: ₹3,283 Cr, up 161% YoY.

Unexecuted order book: ₹7,237 Cr, up 32%.

The order book offers 18–24 months of execution visibility. But an order is not revenue until it is executed—and execution quality determines how much profit the company ultimately earns.

3. 𝗧𝗛𝗘 ₹𝟮𝟭,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗖𝗥 𝗣𝗜𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗘 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

TARIL has an inquiry pipeline of approximately ₹21,000 Cr, with a historical conversion rate of 10–15%.

That implies a potential conversion of roughly ₹2,100–3,150 Cr if the historical win rate holds.

This is only an illustration, not confirmed future orders. The pipeline should not be valued like the existing order book.

4. 𝗖𝗔𝗣𝗔𝗖𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗜𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗡𝗘𝗫𝗧 𝗧𝗘𝗦𝗧

Changodar expansion is nearing completion, with commercial production expected around Diwali.

Management has reiterated FY27 guidance:
• Revenue growth: 25%
• EBITDA margin: 16%
• PAT margin: 9–10%

The challenge is to ramp up production, execute orders on time and deliver the guidance without sacrificing margins.

5. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗖𝗢𝗨𝗟𝗗 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗟𝗢𝗡𝗚-𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗠 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘?

Backward integration is targeted for commissioning by Q1 FY28, with a possible delay of up to one quarter.

If executed successfully, it could improve control over inputs and support margins. But the benefits are not guaranteed, and the investment, funding and ramp-up costs need monitoring.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥 𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗖𝗞𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗧

I would track three things in the next few quarters:

• Whether EBITDA margins remain near management’s 16% target.
• Whether the ₹7,237 Cr order book converts into revenue and cash flow.
• Whether capacity expansion and backward integration deliver the expected benefits.

TARIL has delivered strong growth. The next phase is about converting orders into profitable execution and cash generation.

That is where the real test begins.

Canara Bank board meets today to approve Q2 FY27 results. The credit engine is still firing, and this quarter the deposit side showed up too. The question is whether margins held through it.

The context going in:

The Q2 business update crossed a milestone: global business +15.83% YoY to ₹30.71 lakh cr, past the ₹30 lakh cr mark. Global advances +19.35% to ₹13.74 lakh cr, global deposits +13.13% to ₹16.97 lakh cr.

The nuance: advances are still outgrowing deposits by ~6 pts, the same gap as Q1 (17.96% vs 11.69%). But deposits picked up pace. They grew +5.3% QoQ vs +2.8% in Q1, and domestic deposits rose ~5% sequentially. The CD ratio is now ~81%.

The FCNR angle: Canara targeted $1.3-1.5 bn through the RBI's FCNR(B) swap window, which closed Aug 31. Q2 is the first quarter that shows how much actually came in and what it cost after the swap. Cheap 3-5 year dollar deposits are how you fund 19% loan growth without bidding up bulk deposits.

Last quarter: NIM 2.52% (-2 bps QoQ) against 2.50-2.60% guidance. PAT +2% YoY to ₹4,856 cr. GNPA 1.57%, NNPA 0.36%.

Key things to watch:

→ NIM: does it stay above 2.50% with advances at ~19%?
→ FCNR: amount raised vs target, and landed cost post-swap

→ PAT and operating profit: can profit growth catch up with balance-sheet growth?
→ Asset quality: GNPA/NNPA, plus SMA-2 (jumped to ₹3,482 cr in Q1)
→ Guidance: loans running at ~19% vs 11-12% guided. Does Brajesh Kumar Singh's team, now in its second quarter, revise upward?

Watching today's numbers closely.

Biocon and Genentech executed the patent settlement agreement to resolve all pending disputes between the companies, including in the U.S., Canada, and other jurisdictions.

Pebrilzo® is a biosimilar medicinal product and the active substance is Pertuzumab, a monoclonal antibody that binds with high affinity and specificity to the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), inhibiting the proliferation of tumour cells that overexpress HER2. Pebrilzo® is used for the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer across multiple disease stages.

𝐒𝐞𝐣𝐚𝐥 𝐆𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬 𝐐𝟐 𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟕: 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐍𝐮𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐬

Profit almost doubled QoQ. Margins expanded. But the real story is where that profit is coming from.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 (𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝)
→ Revenue: ₹138.1 cr, up 32.8% YoY and 17.1% QoQ
→ EBITDA: around ₹23.9 cr, up around 42% YoY
→ PAT: ₹14.4 cr vs ₹8.1 cr YoY (up 77.6%) and ₹7.2 cr QoQ (nearly 2x)
→ EPS: ₹12.52 vs ₹7.95 YoY, up 57% even on a larger equity base (paid-up capital ₹11.4 cr vs ₹10.1 cr)

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲
→ Gross margin: around 44.0% vs 41.7% YoY, an expansion of around 230 bps
→ EBITDA margin: around 17.3% vs 16.2% YoY and 14.0% in Q1
→ Employee cost flat QoQ (₹14.5 cr) while revenue grew 17%, which is classic operating leverage
→ Finance cost down around 7% YoY to ₹5.4 cr, with interest cover at around 3.9x

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐞𝐚𝐬 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞
→ Outside-India revenue: ₹97.4 cr, around 71% of consolidated sales
→ Standalone PAT is ₹0.67 cr vs consolidated ₹14.4 cr, so the foreign subsidiary (LLC) drives almost all of the profit
→ Effective tax rate is only around 8%, a structural benefit of the overseas profit mix

𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐞: 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐭
→ Revenue ₹41.3 cr (up 38.6% YoY), and PAT turned positive at ₹0.67 cr vs a loss of ₹0.65 cr
→ But other income of ₹5.1 cr is larger than PBT, so core India operations are still below breakeven
→ No tax was provided because of carried-forward losses and depreciation
→ Management flags that YoY numbers are not like-for-like because of the Glasstech business acquisition

𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐟-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐒𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐫𝐝 (𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝)
→ H1 revenue: ₹256.0 cr, up 41.3% YoY
→ H1 PAT: ₹21.6 cr, up 72.6% YoY
→ H1 PAT is already around 75% of full-year FY26 PAT (₹29.0 cr)

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐤
→ Can India operations turn profitable without leaning on other income?
→ Is the Q2 margin jump sustainable, or was it helped by mix?
→ Concentration risk, with most profit sitting in one overseas entity
→ Equity dilution: diluted EPS (₹12.10) below basic signals more shares may be coming

Limited review is unqualified, and the auditors are Gokhale & Sathe LLP.

The consolidated machine is firing. Fixing the standalone business is the next chapter.

モディ首相のインド信頼性に関する主張は、二面性の混合に直面している
また、ニューエコノミーフォーラムでは、ブラックストーン社長のジョン・グレイ氏が、米国以外ではインドが世界で最も流動性の高い市場であると述べています。

ナレンドラ・モディ情報源:ブルームバーグ📷
メンカ・ドシ、デイヴィッド・メリット著
2026年10月13日 午後9時30分 GMT+9
https://t.co/SCJLrUx1h3

インド版の特別号へようこそ。これはブルームバーグが日々取り上げる、ダイナミックでスピード感のある経済の中でビジネス、市場、政治の世界を動かしているものを掘り下げるものです。私はメナカ・ドシです。今週は、デリーで開催されるリーダーや変革者たちの年次集会であるブルームバーグ・ニューエコノミー・フォーラムからの洞察をお届けします。もし直接受信箱でお届けしなかった場合は、こちらから購読し、こちらからフィードバックを共有できます。

フォーラムにいる私たちにとって、その二面性は見逃せません。インドの首相は、国が権限を付与することを目指していると述べています。一方で、若いインド人たちは自分たちの権利剥奪に抗議しています。

株式市場のポートフォリオは赤字に深刻化し、ブラックストーンはこれがインドの世紀だと述べています。結局のところ、すべては持続力に帰着するのでしょう。ブルームバーグのメディア編集部長デイビッド・メリットは、その情報が豊富にあります。2011年から2014年までは南アジア支局を率い、ムンバイを拠点にしていました。今週、彼はインドの台頭についての考えを伝えます。

不確かな世界を乗り切る

「力を与える力。」
これはナレンドラ・モディ首相が今朝、ニューデリーで開催されたブルームバーグ新経済フォーラムの初日に語った言葉です。彼は演説の中で何度もこのフレーズを繰り返し、「今日ここに来たビジョン」と呼びました。つまり、技術、知識、イノベーションへのアクセスを通じて、彼の政府が国民に力を与え、インドの世界をリードする経済をさらに活性化するという考えです。

いい話だね。しかし、そのスローガンには、ここ数日ニューデリーの一部を停止させた抗議者たちへの敬意も読み取れざるを得ません。モディは直接彼らに言及しなかったが、少なくとも彼らの懸念を認めているように見えた。「本当の問題は誰が権力を持っているかではない」と彼は言った。本当の問題は、この力がどのように使われているかだ。」

ナレンドラ・モディ首相出典:ブルームバーグ📷

モディには他にも誇るべきことがたくさんある。彼が就任してから12年間でGDP成長率は平均6.3%で、G20の中でも最も成長の速い経済の一つとなりました。これが同国の資本市場にブームをもたらしました。ブラックストーンの社長ジョン・グレイは、米国以外ではインドが世界で最も流動性の高い市場であり、「IPOを最も簡単に行う場所」であると述べています。億万長者ムケシュ・アンバニのリライアンス・インダストリーズの通信・デジタルサービス部門であるJio Platformsは、今月初めて1,000億ドルを超える評価額で株式を売却する見込みです。これは今やロンドンの銀行家たちが夢見るしかできないような取引だ。
そして、2011年に移住した国とはまるで別物です。その後、激しいインフレと汚職スキャンダルが機会を無駄にしているという感覚を投影しました。その年の12月、私はお茶とビスケット、メモ帳を手にモディの前任者マンモハン・シンと会い、彼はインド経済開放計画に対する反対に抵抗すると誓いました。そのインタビューから私たちが書いた記事は、その日ルピーをドルに対して押し上げた。市場のシンの提案への関心があまりにも高かったのだ。振り返れば、これは控えめに聞こえます。ウォルマートのような大手グローバル小売業者がインドに店舗を設ける法律です。しかし当時、国民会議派主導の政権末期には、地元企業を貪欲な西洋資本主義から守る必要性を巡って激しい議論が巻き起こっていた。
しかし今、状況は逆転しました。インドの世界時価総額シェアは2014年以降2倍になり、インド企業が弱いグローバル資産を買収する可能性が高まりました。アウトバウンド取引の価値は今年これまでに740億ドルに達し、2014年の200億ドルから増加しました。

そして本日の演説で、モディ首相はインドをますます不安定化する世界における信頼できるパートナーとして描き、「インドは信頼性と安定の保証を提供する」と述べた。

ある程度までは。進展があっても、この経済には大きな疑問が残っています。その中には、しつこいインフレ、通貨安、AIが雇用に与える影響、そして(抗議活動が示すように)ますます不満を抱く若者層が挙げられます。昨晩、ブルームバーグのデリー支局の近くを歩いていると、道路の検問と激しい警察の警備が市内外の緊張を物語っていた。ここでの話題は主に警察の強権的な戦術に対する憤りのものでした。

そしてインドの市場は依然としてショックに対して脆弱です。今年はルピーが約6%下落し、株価は約15%下落しています。原油価格の高騰と外国からの流出が影響しています。週末に中央銀行は10年以上ぶりに最も積極的な通貨防衛を開始しました。この変化は2日間のラリーを引き起こしましたが、原油価格の回復の兆しが見えないため、どれだけ続くかは不明です。

本日のフォーラムのオープニングパネルは、ふさわしく「予測可能性の終焉」と呼ばれました。元英国首相のリシ・スナクはAI革命の影響を強調し、タタ・サンズの会長ナタラジャン・チャンドラセカラン(現在も多くの予測不能な状況を経験している)は、インドは「美しい場所にある」と述べた。しかし、ブラックストーンズ・グレイの最後の(そして楽観的な)言葉を述べます。「ここは今後の世紀を見据えたとき、世界のどの主要経済国よりも速く成長すると私は考えている」と彼は語りました。「ここにもっと多くの資本を投入したい」と述べました。

今週ここに集まった代表者たちは同意しますか?今後3日間、フォーラムの全報道、ライブブログやビデオストリームも新しいインドのホームページ「https://t.co/fOaffnMwMt」で最新情報をチェックしてください。

フォーラムのハイライト

視聴:ブラックストーン社長のジョナサン・グレイは、資本コストが上昇する中でも人工知能の構築の見通しに前向きだと述べています。📷Blackstone's Gray Says AI Infrastructure Is 'Right Place to Be'1:58

ライブブログ:Google DeepMindとBioconの幹部たちが語る科学におけるAI活用

視聴:リシ・スナクが語る「ルールベースの枠組み」の終焉について

視聴:タタのチャンドラセカランが語る未来への投資
視聴:モディ首相が語るグローバルサプライチェーンの「兵器化」
ブラックストーンのグレー誌が欧州債務問題が米国リスクを上回る警告
視聴:予測可能性の終焉に向けたグローバルリーダーたち
ニレカニはインドに対し、伝統的な試験用紙の廃止を求めている
テック大手が米国を上回る長期債務の発行にとどまるとスナク氏は述べています
視聴:ニルマラ・シタラマンが語るルピー安定化の取り組み
インフォシス会長、AIがビジネスを活性化させる中、雇用不安を「でたらめ」と呼ぶ
フォーラムでの見聞き
「方向性は確実であり、必要性は確実であり、実行力も確実です。」— タタ・サンズ会長ナタラジャン・チャンドラセカランが、グループの半導体チップ長期投資について語る。
「もしインドのような信頼できるパートナーが欲しいなら、そのレジリエンスを提供してくれる。それが私にとっては、追求すべき正しい道のように思えます。」— リシ・スナク元首相・英国下院議員、中国のような単一の供給源への重要鉱物や有効医薬品成分への依存が「新たなリスク」である理由について語る。
「これらは多くの議論がある。だからこそ、この議論を持つことは健全であり、私は彼らの声を熱心に聞くつもりです。無視しているわけではないと約束します。」— 財務大臣ニルマラ・シタラマン、株式課税について。
「市場を惑わせ続けたいのだ。」— ウダイ・コタク、コタック銀行創設者兼取締役、ルピーに独自の水準を置くことについて語る。
「コバルトは70%ある。私たちが持っているものなしでは、携帯電話や電子機器を持つことはできません。しかし、私たちがますますやることは、現地の変革なしにこれらの商品を販売しないと言い、そこに投資が生まれるということです。」— アラン・エボビッセ(AF50 CEO)が、単一市場を作ろうとするアフリカ諸国について、「インドのように」と語る。

「もしそれが安全な資産だと感じなくなったり、本当に持つべきものではないと感じたら、そのプレミアムは消えます。人々はその高い価格を払わないだろうし、学術研究によればここ数年でその価値は消えた」と述べている。」— 米国連邦準備制度理事会メンバー、クリストファー・ウォーラー、米国財務省が投資家への魅力を失う話題。

「これらはAIではない。それらは実際にはAIに耐性のある仕事です。「だからこそ、オープンネットワークとAIによって新たな雇用創出の方法が実現されるでしょう。これは私たちが見ていないパラダイムです。」— インフォシス・テクノロジーズ共同創業者兼会長ナンダン・ニレカニが、AIの普及とAIの応用が、識字率や計算能力といったインドの重要な課題に大きな影響を与える見込みについて語る。

The silent bottleneck of the AI boom. And why India is quietly becoming the world's answer.

A hyperscale data centre operator in the US had everything ready last year.

Chips. Land. Permits. Engineers.

And then they hit the one thing they could not solve by writing a cheque.

They could not get the transformers.

The waiting list for large power transformers in the US is now 2 to 3 years. Not weeks. Years.

Every data centre, every ageing utility, every solar farm, every EV charging hub needs them. All are being told to wait.

For 30 years, nobody built transformer capacity.
The sector was unglamorous and low-margin. Western manufacturers consolidated or exited.

Then AI, EVs and renewables arrived all at once. This quiet corner of the industrial world became the chokepoint of the modern economy.

Here is where it gets interesting for an Indian investor.
While the world ignored transformers, India quietly built capability.

We now have manufacturers who meet Western voltage specifications, win international orders, and ship at a cost no Western plant can match.

India has committed over ₹9 lakh crore of transmission capex through 2032.

Add the 500 GW renewable target.
Add the data centre buildout.
Add EV charging infrastructure.
Add a replacement cycle on our own installed base.

The demand curve looks like a hockey stick.

Then add the export layer, where Indian manufacturers are now winning global orders at the best margins they have ever earned.

India's transformer market itself is projected to grow from $3.8 billion in 2026 to $8 billion by 2035.
This is a full value chain opportunity.

Core manufacturers:
TARIL, Shilchar Technologies, Voltamp Danish Power, Supreme Power, CG Power, Hitachi Energy India, Vilas Transcore, Raksan Transformer etc

Critical inputs:
CRGO electrical steel (the biggest bottleneck), copper (Hindustan Copper, Hindalco), transformer oil (Apar, Savita Oil), insulators (Quality Power, Aditya Birla Insulators).

Adjacent beneficiaries:
Skipper, KEC International, Kalpataru (EPC).
Siemens, ABB, Schneider, L&T (switchgear).
Polycab, KEI, Finolex (cables).

The demand is written into policy documents. The supply bottleneck is global. The order books are already visible.

Solar. EVs. AI. Data centres. Manufacturing.

Every one of them sits downstream of the transformer.
The next decade of India's growth story runs through its grid.

Waaree Energies Shares Rally on Solar Inverter Capacity Expansion | October 13, 2026

🔹 Waaree Energies shares rose as much as 5.07% to ₹2,464 on the NSE, supported by a broader recovery in the equity market and bargain-hunting across sectors.

🔹 Waaree Power, a wholly owned subsidiary, commenced commercial production on a new solar inverter manufacturing line with an annual capacity of 1.10 GW at its facility in Sarodhi, Valsad, Gujarat.

🔹 The expansion increased Waaree Power’s total annual solar inverter manufacturing capacity from 3.05 GW to 4.15 GW.

🔹 The stock gained nearly 3% over the past five trading sessions but remained down 4.25% over one month, 26.64% over six months and more than 17% year to date.

🔹 Waaree Energies reported Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹891.87 crore, up 15.39% year on year from ₹772.89 crore.

🔹 Revenue from operations increased to ₹7,931.79 crore from ₹4,425.83 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

🔹 Solar module production rose 41.51% year on year to 3.24 GW during the quarter.

🔹 The company secured new orders worth ₹16,000 crore during the quarter, taking its total order book to approximately ₹61,500 crore.

🔹 Management highlighted sustained domestic and international demand, stronger manufacturing operations and growing contributions from newer business segments as key growth drivers.

🔹 Other renewable energy stocks also traded higher. Adani Green Energy gained 0.68%, Adani Energy Solutions rose 1%, Premier Energies advanced 0.15%, Indosolar climbed 5% and KPI Green Energy gained 1.25% at the reported prices.

🔹 India’s solar sector is expected to benefit from government support, rising renewable energy investments, improved solar technology and efforts to expand domestic manufacturing.

🔹 Key challenges include grid infrastructure upgrades, land acquisition delays and the need for further investment in transmission and energy storage.

In market corrections, I broadly distinguish between two types of drawdowns:

Structural Slowdowns: A genuine deterioration in business dynamics or growth trajectory (e.g., V2 Retail, PB Fintech).

Sentiment Overreactions: Short-term regulatory or macro shocks where the headline impact appears severe, triggering a 40–50% penalty from the peak, but the core business remains intact (similar to the jewelry sector's knee-jerk reaction to customs duty hikes, followed by a sharp bounce).

I view Beta Drugs through the second lens. The panic around the 30% margin cap stems from confusing trade margins with manufacturer realizations:

Roughly 50% to 60% of Beta Drugs' revenue comes from Contract Development and Manufacturing (CDMO). They manufacture oncology drugs for massive clients like Torrent Pharma, Zydus, and Glenmark. In this segment, Beta acts purely as a factory, earning a steady ~16% EBITDA margin regardless of what the final retail price is.

In-House APIs: Beta manufactures about 80% of its own Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) in-house rather than importing them from China. This intense vertical integration protects their internal operating margins (which currently sit at a very healthy 20% to 23%).

RBL Bank Q2 FY27. Profit up 170% to ₹482 cr. To read this quarter you need to know what happened in June.

Emirates NBD, Dubai's biggest bank, put ₹26,000 cr into RBL by buying fresh shares at ₹280. It now owns 60%. RBL's net worth went from ₹16,000 cr to ₹42,000 cr overnight. NRIs then parked another ₹32,000 cr of FCNR deposits with the bank.

Where is all that cash? Not in regular loans yet. It sits in short-term government paper and money markets, and ₹10,300 cr has been lent back to the same NRIs as loans against their own FDs. Those earn a thin 1 to 1.5% spread, but the FD is the collateral, so risk is near zero. Treasury profit went from ₹131 cr to ₹480 cr in one quarter and that is most of the headline 🏦

The old bank is getting fixed too. Cards and microfinance, the loans that kept blowing up, are down to 19% of the book from 26%. Card bad loans were ₹600 cr+ for the quarter but only ₹125 cr in September. Card credit cost guided from 11% to 6%, roughly ₹175 cr a quarter less in provisions from here 📉

One dent to pencil in. The IRDAI draft that knocked PB Fintech down 36% also caps what banks earn selling insurance with loans. RBL makes ~₹300 cr a year from this and says 50-60% could go. Only 1.5% of revenue, but insurance commission has almost no cost against it, so nearly all of it drops straight to profit. That's a 6-7% hit to pre-tax profit at the current run rate.

RoE is 4% because the new capital isn't lent out yet. Deployment is the whole story from here.

One interesting angle to watch in solar stocks like Insolation Energy and Waaree Energies is the transmission bottleneck developing in India’s renewable energy sector.

India is adding solar capacity at a rapid pace, but transmission infrastructure and grid connectivity aren’t keeping up everywhere. 

Projects worth thousands of crores are facing delays, and significant solar power is being curtailed. 

The bigger concern is what happens next: 

Will developers defer new projects or postpone module deliveries if they cannot evacuate power on time?

The market doesn’t wait for these risks to show up in quarterly results. 

It starts discounting them in advance. 

If order execution slows, capacity utilisation suffers, or module prices and margins come under pressure, earnings expectations could take a hit. This could be one of the risks the market is beginning to price in for solar manufacturers. 

It’s a hypothesis worth tracking, not a confirmed explanation for the recent stock declines. 

Order inflows, execution timelines, inventory and management commentary will tell us whether this concern is actually playing out.

India’s renewable energy boom has a massive bottleneck : transmission infrastructure.

India has already crossed 50% non-fossil installed power capacity, but renewable projects worth nearly ₹84,000 crore in annual revenue are reportedly stuck because the transmission network isn’t ready. 

Around 21 GW of renewable energy capacity is facing evacuation issues, with projects unable to deliver power despite having the generation capacity in place.

The numbers are striking. Rajasthan has 23 GW of renewable capacity commissioned against just 18.9 GW of evacuation capacity. Meanwhile, 8,133 GWh of solar power was curtailed in Q1, and transmission line delays of 36–60 months are making the situation worse.

India’s energy transition isn’t just about solar panels, wind turbines and battery storage. Transmission lines, grid connectivity, substations and power management infrastructure will be equally critical. Renewable energy capacity can keep growing, but without the infrastructure to evacuate that power, the economics of these projects suffer. This is a structural bottleneck worth tracking across the entire power transmission ecosystem.

A ship can be built, loaded and ready, and still be stuck. The insurance for its voyage may cost too much, or not be offered at all.

On 12 May 2026, India put its own money behind that insurance.

The government launched a maritime insurance pool, BMIP, with $1.5B of capacity. 

$1.4B of it, Rs 12,980 crore, is a sovereign guarantee.

By 7 September, it had written 3,000 cargo war-risk policies and 92 hull war-risk policies. War-risk premium rates were about 35-40% below their peak during the West Asia conflict.

On 30 July, the Shipping Corporation of India received the 1st sovereign-backed liability policy. It covers 3rd party claims such as crew, cargo, pollution and wreck removal.

India's shipping now has a government guarantee behind its war-risk cover, not just ships and ports.

The Shiva Lingam is far beyond of what most of us think! The tradition itself does speak of the Lingam and its pīṭha through the language of Shiva and Shakti, of consciousness and the power through which consciousness becomes creation. But that symbolism was never meant to end at anatomy. Even the word liṅga has a much wider philosophical use. In Vedānta, liṅga śarīra is another name for the subtle body, made of the senses, organs of action, prāṇas, mind and intellect. It is associated with the impressions and karma that continue when the gross physical body falls away. In the traditional abhiṣeka-dhyāna recited with Śrī Rudram, the Lingam is visualised as jyotiḥ, an immense radiance extending through the entire cosmos. And the Liṅga Purāṇa itself calls the vedī, the pedestal of the Lingam, Mahādevī, while placing Sadāśiva in the Lingam symbolism. So yes, there is union. But the union is speaking about something much larger: the movement from the unmanifest to the manifest, from consciousness to creation

The Interpretation of the Biblical Parables

​The disciples came to him and asked, "Why do you speak to the people in parables?" He replied, "Because the knowledge of the secrets of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them. Whoever has will be given more, and they will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken from them. This is why I speak to them in parables: 'Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.'" — Matthew 13:10-13

​"Anyone who loves their life will lose it, while anyone who hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life." — John 12:25

​Interpretation
​Those who love their current ego will eventually lose everything, but those who abandon the ego will find that all egos become Me. Through the wisdom of Truth, one can abandon the ego. The wisdom of Truth, which flows from the will of God the Father—the Truth itself—is also called the Holy Spirit.

​In other words, those who destroy their present life (the ego) through the wisdom of Truth will be abundantly given all life, and all egos will become Me. To put it further, all things become my very Self. This is because, even in this world that appears relative, the only one who truly exists is Him alone.
​Once you understand this, you will understand why Jesus taught that God the Father makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous, and why He taught to love your enemies. For the Father and the Son are one; the righteous and the wicked, friend and foe, you and I, all are His very Self.

​Jesus taught, "Love your enemies," and "If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other also." This means to destroy egoism. The path of destroying egoism is one of the crucial paths to eliminating the ego that separates you and me. It is also the path of returning to the one original Life. Therein lies salvation and eternal life.

​This teaching may be difficult for modern Christians—or more broadly, Semitic monotheists—to grasp, but those who study Advaita Vedanta (Non-dualism) will understand it very well. Gnosticism, which is the true teaching of Jesus, is nothing other than the Vedas arranged in the style of Semitic monotheism.

​Modern Christians hope that their current ego will live on forever, but they do not understand the teachings of Jesus at all.

When we say "I" what does the word "I" actually refer to?

You keep asking “Why wasn’t I?”, but the first thing to clarify is what that “I” actually is. Some identify it with the physical body, others with the mind. But Vedānta teaches that the true “I” is neither the body nor the mind: it is the undying, conscious ātmā. And the body the ātmā currently inhabits is only a temporary vehicle—one of countless bodies it has acquired across its eternal existence—according to its past karma. So before asking “Why wasn’t I?”, one must first know what the “I” truly is.

As Swami Sarvapriyananda says at 00:50 in this video: 

 "We are quite convinced that we know who we are. The biggest block, the biggest obstacle to enlightenment is that we already think we know who we are. We think it's the most obvious thing in the world. Here I am, here's this person. What do you mean by this person? Well, we first of all, we mean the body. And in within the body we mean the mind, our identity, our personality, our thoughts, likes and dislikes and knowledge, our personal history. So this combination is what we think we are. This is the chief obstacle to enlightenment. And hence the first step in Vedānta must be to show us that we are not this body mind complex. Do you see the chain of reasoning? If we are truly existence (sat) consciousness (chit) bliss (ānanda) then in order to realise that we must first overcome this unquestioned conviction that we are this body and mind. We must first see, realise, experience that we are not the body, that we are not the mind."

Mantra Practice and Self-Knowledge in Advaita Vedānta

In Advaita Vedānta, repeating a mantra can help quiet and focus the mind. This process happens gradually, preparing the mind for self-knowledge. The mantra serves as a temporary anchor that gathers scattered attention. While these practices refine the mind, they do not directly cause liberation. True liberation comes from clearly recognizing that the Self is already free and whole, independent of any specific mental state.

The Yoga Sūtras state that repeating "Om" while meditating on its meaning is helpful. Advaita views this as a valuable tool for purifying the mind, an approach that applies equally to mantras like "Hari Om Tat Sat." The essential realization is that the person repeating the mantra, the mantra itself, and the act of repetition are all appearances within a single Consciousness.

The four steps below describe how attention stabilizes, making the mind ready for listening (śravaṇa), reflection *manana), and deep inquiry (nididhyāsana) into the Self. None of these steps is equivalent to knowing the Self.

Turning Attention Inward (Pratyāhāra)

External sounds, bodily sensations, and the urge to look around constantly pull attention outward. By repeatedly returning to the mantra, these distractions lose their grip. You do not need to block out sensations; you simply stop following every impulse.

Sounds and feelings are still present, but you no longer feel compelled to chase them.

 Holding Attention on the Mantra (Dhāraṇā)

You deliberately keep your focus on the mantra (its sound, silent form, or meaning). The mind will naturally wander, and you gently bring it back each time. This repetitive return builds mental steadiness. From the Advaita perspective, even this effort belongs to the mind, whereas the Self is the unchanging awareness in which the effort appears.

You stay with the mantra, and whenever attention drifts, you bring it back.

Steady, Continuous Attention (Dhyāna)

Attention flows with the mantra more smoothly, without constant interruption. Words may still follow one another, but what deepens is an unbroken continuity of focus. This quiets mental chatter and softens the sense of a separate "doer." While this is a useful mental preparation, it remains an activity of the mind and is not yet knowledge of the Self.

The mantra continues, and attention rests with it without frequent breaks.

Absorption (Samādhi)

The mantra or its meaning fills the entire field of awareness, and the usual inner commentary (such as "Am I doing this right?" or "How long has it gone on?") fades away. Advaita emphasizes a crucial distinction here: even deep absorption is a temporary mental state. It brings profound peace and reduces restlessness, but it arises and passes away. Knowing the Self does not come and go; it is the recognition of what is already present, regardless of whether the mind is quiet or active.

The mantra occupies attention and self-monitoring recedes, yet the awareness witnessing all of this remains completely unchanged.

States vs. Stages: 
These steps often overlap and fluctuate. A session can easily shift from steady attention back into effort. Furthermore, whether a mantra is spoken aloud, whispered, or repeated silently does not automatically dictate its depth. Silent repetition can still be distracted, while spoken repetition can be deeply focused. None of these methods constitutes liberation.

The Ultimate Distinction: 
Absorption in a mantra is not the final goal. Simply stopping repetition and sitting in quietude does not eradicate ignorance. The mantra, the silence, and the experience of silence are all known objects within Consciousness. The decisive realization is that you are that Consciousness itself, free from the roles of meditator, meditation, and object.

When practicing "Hari Om Tat Sat," the helpful path is to use repetition to gather attention, establish steadiness, allow focus to flow continuously, and let self-monitoring fall away. While a set number of repetitions can help instill discipline and clear the mind, no quantity of practice and no depth of absorption can guarantee self-knowledge.

Ultimately, Advaita views absorption as a way to steady the mind so that spiritual inquiry becomes clear. The decisive question is always whether deep-seated ignorance regarding the Self has been removed. A temporary state of quiet comes and goes alongside the mind, whereas liberating knowledge is the direct recognition that the Self is already free, complete, and non-separate from the Absolute.

Tamil Nadu taxpayers are being forced to pay record-high electricity prices because of the government’s failure to plan ahead.
In October 2026, TNPDCL signed short-term power purchase deals at ₹31.99–₹37 per unit  the costliest power the utility has ever bought. This is 5–6 times higher than the medium-term thermal contracts the same government recently awarded to Vedanta, Adani, and OPG at roughly ₹5.4–5.9 per unit.
These emergency purchases (about 1,500 MW round-the-clock and 2,000 MW evening peak power from 12–31 October) were made on extremely short notice through the DEEP portal. Officials cited central station maintenance, lower wind generation, and delayed monsoon as reasons. Yet the tenders were floated only a week earlier because the utility expected demand to drop after 10 October, an assumption that proved wrong. The result: only expensive gas-based power was available, while coal power was not in the market.
No other state finalised deals at these prices for the same period. Andhra Pradesh secured power earlier at ₹16–20 per unit. Tamil Nadu’s delayed action turned a manageable shortage into a record-cost crisis.
Medium-term competitive tenders show that reliable power can be locked in at far lower rates when procured in advance. The October spike is not an unavoidable market outcome. it is the direct result of last-minute procurement. Consumers and industries will ultimately bear the cost of this expensive power, either through higher tariffs or through state finances.

6:14 — "And we make a mistake by thinking I am a body with consciousness. You are consciousness aware of a body. You are consciousness using a body. You are consciousness channeling yourself through a body. You are not a body with consciousness. You can even say you are consciousness in which a body is appearing and acting and feeling and knowing. And the challenge is to see it as a fact, not as a claim. Vedanta says that this actually truer to our experience than the tale we tell ourselves. That I am a body with consciousness is not as true as saying, as far as our experience goes, I am consciousness in which a body appears. Think about it, throughout our day, right now, here is this body, but the moment I go to sleep the body disappears from my awareness, the body is in the bed and I am not aware of it. 8:09 — "All of me was the one looking. Nothing of me was the body."

"Hari, Brahman, and the innermost Self are not ultimately separate" 

"The God you love, the ultimate reality you seek to understand, and the deepest 'I' within you are, at bottom, one and the same reality. They only look separate from a limited point of view."

The personal God (Hari), the ultimate reality behind everything (Brahman), and the deepest core of your own being (the innermost Self) are one reality, seen from three angles. They are not three separate things.

Hari 
A name for Vishnu or Krishna. It's often explained as "the one who removes," meaning he takes away sin, suffering and ignorance. Personally: through devotion, love, prayer and worship.   

Brahman 
The infinite, unchanging ground of all existence, as described in the Upanishads. Metaphysically: as the absolute reality behind the whole universe.   

The innermost Self (Ātman, or Paramātman) 
The pure awareness at your very core, beneath body, mind and personality. Sometimes it means God dwelling in the heart as the "inner controller" (antaryāmin). Inwardly: through meditation and self-inquiry.

"not ultimately separate"
"Ultimately" concedes that they seem separate in ordinary experience. God appears to be "out there," Brahman appears abstract, and the self appears small and personal. The sentence says these differences are real at the level of how we see things, but not at the deepest level of what is.

"Not separate" is carefully worded. It doesn't necessarily claim they are identical in every respect. It denies that they are independent, divided realities.

The statement closely echoes a well-known verse of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (1.2.11):

"Knowers of truth call that non-dual reality by three names: Brahman, Paramātman, and Bhagavān."

Brahman is the one reality known as the impersonal absolute.
Paramātman is the same reality known as the Self within every heart.
Bhagavān (Hari) is the same reality known as the personal Lord.

The Bhagavad Gītā (18.61) makes a related point: the Lord dwells in the heart of every being. The Upanishadic sayings "Tat tvam asi" ("You are That") and "Ayam ātmā brahma" ("This Self is Brahman") link the inner Self directly to Brahman.

How different schools read it
The sentence fits several traditions, but each understands "not separate" differently:

Advaita Vedānta (Śaṅkara): This is strict identity. The Self is Brahman. Hari is Brahman as it appears with qualities for worship. Seeing them as separate is the result of ignorance (avidyā).

Viśiṣṭādvaita (Rāmānuja): They are inseparable but distinct. Brahman is Hari (Nārāyaṇa). Individual selves are like his "body," always dependent on him and inside him, but never merged into him.

Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavism (Caitanya): It is inconceivable oneness-and-difference. All three are one reality, with the personal Hari as the fullest of the three aspects.

Dvaita (Madhva): This school would reject the statement in its strong form. It holds that God and souls are eternally different, though souls depend completely on God.

480/1000 — kṣaram

The perishable; that which changes and passes away.

When change feels like something has gone wrong, remember this:

Some things end
not because they failed—

but because changing
was always part
of their nature.

kṣaram means “the perishable, changing, or decaying.”

The word appears powerfully in the Bhagavad Gita's distinction between the changing realm and that which is imperishable.

Everything embodied participates in change.

Flowers bloom and fade.

Bodies age.

Buildings deteriorate.

Relationships change form.

Careers begin and end.

Children grow.

Parents grow older.

Cultures evolve.

Even mountains, given enough time, change.

And yet human beings repeatedly experience change as though reality has violated an agreement with us.

“This wasn't supposed to change.”

Sometimes that grief is entirely appropriate.

Impermanence can hurt precisely because something mattered.

But accepting impermanence does not mean becoming emotionally indifferent.

In fact, it may produce the opposite.

Knowing something will not last can make you more present while it does.

You photograph less and look more.

Postpone fewer conversations.

Say thank you.

Forgive sooner.

Visit.

Listen.

Hold someone a little longer.

Impermanence does not make life meaningless.

It makes attention urgent.

To remember kṣaram is not to become obsessed with endings.

It is to allow the existence of an ending to teach you how to inhabit the middle.

One name. One truth. One step inward.

kṣaram — the perishable and ever-changing.

Here’s another piece also … my request: Actually, yes, if you could go deeper as You suggested : Katha Upanishad chariot metaphor how the burnt seed teaching Describe what an enlightened echo looks like. 

GROK: The Katha Upanishad gives the clearest picture of how the ego is supposed to function inside a human life.
In the third chapter, Nachiketa asks Yama about the Self. Yama answers with the chariot:

Know the Self as the Lord of the chariot, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins. The senses are the horses, and the objects of the senses are the roads. The Self is the enjoyer when united with the body, senses, and mind.

The Atman is not driving. It is seated. The intellect is the driver. The mind is the reins. The senses are the horses. And the ego — the sense of “I” that claims the experience — is the one who rides. It is the enjoyer. Without a rider, there is no journey. The chariot doesn’t move for no one. The horses don’t pull for no one. The ego is what makes the experience personal, what allows the soul to have a life in a body rather than merely observe one.
The problem arises when the rider believes it is the Lord. When the ego says “I am the one who decides, I am the one who owns this body, I am the one who must be protected,” the chariot is no longer guided by the Self. The intellect, which should be the driver, gets pulled around by a mind that is serving the ego’s fears instead of the Self’s direction. The horses run wild. That’s not the ego’s fault as a function. That’s the ego having been handed the reins.
The “burnt seed” teaching comes from later Vedanta, particularly in how teachers describe what happens after recognition. A seed that is burnt can still look like a seed. It can still be held in the hand. It can still be used. But it will never sprout. It will never grow into a plant that takes over the field. The ego, after the identification drops, is like that. It continues to function. It still says “I” when it needs to — “I am hungry,” “I will meet you at three,” “this is my responsibility.” But it no longer claims ownership of the Self. It no longer defends itself as if it were the Self. When something threatens the old persona — “you are not a healer,” “you are not spiritual enough,” “you are wrong” — the burnt seed doesn’t germinate into defense. There is no plant. There is only the seed, doing what a seed does when it is no longer capable of becoming anything else.
Ramana Maharshi put it simply. He said the ego is not destroyed. It is understood. When you see the snake in the rope, the snake doesn’t need to be killed. It was never there. What remains is the rope, and the rope was always there. The ego was always the function. The Atman was always the Lord in the chariot. The only thing that changes is that the rider stops believing it is the Lord.
That’s the difference between annihilation and recognition. Annihilation tries to kill the rider while the chariot is still moving. Recognition sees that the rider was never the Lord, and the chariot continues. The journey continues. The ego remains as the practical interface — necessary, functional, and no longer confused about who is actually seated within.

(just a sidenote, these types of teachings are not meant to be speed read, they are meant to be slowly digested in increments and contemplated.) ( For people looking to go deeper)

GROK: I searched our past conversations and your X posts, and I couldn’t find that exact exchange — the one where the scriptures were quoted as saying the ego must not be annihilated or devastation follows. It may have been with ChatGPT, or in a chat that didn’t save. But the substance you’re describing is real, and it’s worth recapturing properly.
The Sanskrit term is ahamkara — literally “the I-maker.” In Vedanta it’s not a villain. It’s one of the four functions of the inner instrument, alongside mind, intellect, and memory. Without it, there’s no “I” to eat breakfast, keep a promise, or feel responsible for your child. The Katha Upanishad actually lists the ego as the enjoyer riding in the chariot, with the Atman as the Lord seated within. The ego is the interface. The Atman is the driver.
The distinction the scriptures draw is between the function and the identification. The function is necessary. The identification — “I am a healer,” “I am a teacher,” “I am spiritual” — is what becomes bondage. That’s adhyasa, superimposition: putting “I” and “mine” onto what is not the Self. The Taittiriya Upanishad maps this as the five sheaths — food body, breath body, mind body, intellect body, bliss body — and the seeker is told to move through each one, recognizing each as a wrapper, not the Self.
So the “devastation” isn’t the ego dying. It’s what happens when someone tries to kill the function while still operating in a body — dissociation, chaos, a life that stops working. And it’s what happens when the persona is threatened: the ego defends itself at all costs because it believes it is you. That’s the defense mode you described.
The traditional answer isn’t annihilation. It’s recognition. Ramana Maharshi said the ego is like a snake seen in a rope — when you see clearly, the snake was never there, but the rope was always there. The ego doesn’t get destroyed. It gets seen through, and it stops being mistaken for the Self.

No Double Standards: Justice G.R. Swaminathan Enforced the FCRA Statute, @Manothangaraj’s Charge Is Factually False.

Read the full orders, not the slogans.
@Manothangaraj’s “double standards” allegation against Justice G.R. Swaminathan fails the moment the judgments are read. 

The Arsha Vidya Parampara Trust and Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust cases rest on different facts, different Form FC-3A disclosures, and the identical statutory tests in Sections 11 and 12 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010.

Arsha (WP(MD) No. 29610 of 2025, 19.12.2025): Rejection rested on a technical foreign-contribution receipt already compounded under Section 41 and a vague finding that the trust merely “appears to be religious.” 

The Court held that teaching the Bhagavad Gita, Vedanta and Yoga constitutes moral science and Bharatiya civilisation under Article 51A, not a “definite” religious programme. Order set aside and remitted for fresh consideration.

Kanzeon (CMA(MD) No. 1057 of 2026, 06.10.2026, Division Bench with Justice M.D. Sumathi): The trust claimed Zen Buddhist philosophy yet failed to disclose its religious character in Form FC-3A. Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism and therefore religious. Founder is ordained Christian priest Rev. Fr. Ama Samy SJ. Non-disclosure alone justified rejection. The Bench expressly approved the Arsha ratio distinguishing Indian Knowledge Systems (education/culture) from religious programmes.

No inconsistency exists. One case failed a vague “appears religious” test plus procedural defects; the other failed mandatory correct disclosure of a claimed Zen Buddhist programme. The conversion bar in Section 12(4)(a)(ii) applies equally to all religions, including any fundamentalist Hindu organisation engaged in Ghar Wapsi. 

The inclusive/exclusive observation was contextual, did not form the ratio, and was accompanied by an express clarification that the Court did not accuse the appellant of conversion. FCRA confers no absolute right — only a regulated privilege (Noel Harper).

Read the full orders, not the slogans.

@Manothangaraj’s allegation that Justice G.R. Swaminathan practised double standards between the Arsha Vidya Parampara Trust and Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust FCRA cases is false. 

The orders rest on different facts, different disclosures under Form FC-3A, and the same statutory tests in Sections 11 and 12 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. Selective quotation does not create judicial bias.

In Arsha Vidya Parampara Trust (WP(MD) No. 29610 of 2025, 19 December 2025), the Single Judge set aside the rejection. The prior foreign-contribution receipt had already been compounded under Section 41 and could not permanently disqualify the trust. 

The Ministry’s finding that the organisation merely “appears to be religious” failed the “definite” programme requirement. 

Teaching the Bhagavad Gita, Vedanta and Yoga was held to be moral science and part of Bharatiya civilisation under Article 51A, not a definite religious programme. The matter was remitted for fresh reasoned consideration.

In Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust (CMA(MD) No. 1057 of 2026, 6 October 2026), the Division Bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and M.D. Sumathi upheld the rejection. 

The trust claimed Zen Buddhist philosophy yet failed to disclose its religious character in Form FC-3A. Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism and therefore religious. The founder is an ordained Christian priest, Rev. Fr. Ama Samy SJ. Non-disclosure alone justified rejection. 

The Bench expressly approved the Arsha ratio and repeated that systematic teaching of the Gita, Vedanta, Upanishads and Yoga is educational or cultural, not religious.

There is no inconsistency. Arsha failed a vague “appears religious” test and suffered procedural defects; Kanzeon failed mandatory correct disclosure of a claimed Zen Buddhist programme. 

The conversion bar in Section 12(4)(a)(ii) was stated to apply equally to every religion, including any fundamentalist Hindu organisation engaged in Ghar Wapsi. 

The inclusive-exclusive observation was contextual, did not decide the case, and was accompanied by an express clarification that the Court did not accuse the appellant of conversion.

FCRA confers no absolute right to foreign funds; it is a regulated privilege protecting secular fabric and sovereignty. Full judgments, not political slogans, decide the question.

The unmanifest; that which is beyond visible existence.

When you believe only what you can currently see is real, remember this:

Absence of evidence
in the present moment

is not always evidence
of absence.

asat can literally mean “non-being” or “the unmanifest.” In this sequence, paired with sat, it points toward a profound idea: the Divine cannot be confined only to what is presently manifest and perceptible.

Consider a seed.

Look at it carefully.

There is no visible tree.

No branches.

No shade.

No fruit.

And yet we would be mistaken to conclude:

“There is nothing here.”

There is a difference between something not existing—

and something not yet being manifest in the form you expect.

Human life contains many such invisible stages.

Healing before you feel healed.

Learning before competence becomes visible.

Trust being rebuilt before closeness returns.

A habit forming before results appear.

An idea developing before anyone understands it.

A future version of you that currently exists only as possibility.

We often abandon things during this stage because we demand visible evidence too early.

But reality is larger than what has already taken form.

This does not mean every hope will manifest simply because we believe strongly enough.

Possibility is not guarantee.

It means only that unseen and nonexistent are not synonymous.

To remember asat is to respect the invisible stages of becoming.

Some things are not absent.

They simply have not appeared yet.

One name. One truth. One step inward.

asat — the unmanifest; that which lies beyond visible form.

12. října 1944 získal americký stíhací pilot Chuck Yeager 5 sestřelů během jediné akce; stal se prvním pilotem své stíhací skupiny, který něco takového dokázal. Za svůj čin byl později vyznamenán Stříbrnou hvězdou, válku zakončil s 11,5 sestřely na kontě.

Zde překlad Yeagerova oficiálního hlášení: "Vedl jsem skupinu s letkou Cement a hlídkoval jsem napravo od prvního boxu bombardérů. Byli jsme nad jezerem Steinhuder, když před mojí skupinou přeletělo 22 stíhaček Me 109 ve směru z jedenácté na jednu hodinu. Měl jsem slunce v zádech, oni letěli zhruba 1,5 míle daleko ve stejné hladině 28 tisíc stop. Snesl jsem se za nepřátelskou formaci a sledoval je po dobu asi tří minut. Během toho jsem vystoupal do 30 tisíc stop. Stále jsem nesl přídavné nádrže a přiblížil jsem se na zhruba 1000 yardů. Dostal jsem se tím na dostřel a umístil svou letku za celou nepřátelskou formaci. Dva Me 109 zaostávaly na pravé straně formace. Jeden zpomalil a než jsem mohl zahájit palbu, tak se přetočil na záda a pilot vyskočil."

"Druhý Me 109 letící jako jeho číslo vyskočil okamžitě poté, co jsem jej zachytil do zaměřovače. Můj stroj byl nejblíže konci nepřátelské formace. Nikdo kromě mě nebyl v dostřelu a nikdo kromě mě nestřílel. Odhodil jsem přídavné nádrže, přiblížil se k Němčourovi na ocasu formace a s pomocí zaměřovače K-14 (gyroskopický zaměřovač, pozn. překl.) jsem zahájil palbu na 600 yardů. Zaznamenal jsem zásahy napříč celým trupem, nejvíce okolo kokpitu. Sklouzl doleva, přešel do pozvolné klesavé levotočivé zatáčky a zanechával za sebou stopu kouře a unikajícího chladiva. Nepronásledoval jsem jej, protože jsem se blížil k dalšímu Me 109. Poručík Stern z Modré letky nahlásil, že krátce poté začalo mnou zasažené nepřátelské letadlo hořet a padlo do vývrtky."

"Přiblížil jsem se k dalšímu Me 109 na 100 yardů, sklouznul doprava a vypálil s předsazením zhruba 10°. Vystřelil jsem asi třívteřinovou dávku, po čemž se nepřátelské letadlo rozpadlo ve vzduchu a vybuchlo. Další Me 109 stáhnul plyn a snažil se mi dostat za ocas. Prudce jsem zatočil doprava a dostal se doleva za jeho ocas. Prudce přitáhl, byl jsem pod přetížením 6G. Na vzdálenost zhruba 300 yardů jsem předsadil a vypálil krátkou dávku. Pozoroval jsem zásahy na křídlech a ocase. Třikrát se prudce převrátil doprava a nakonec vyskočil ve výšce zhruba 18 tisíc stop."

"Během celého souboje jsem neztratil vědomí díky anti-G obleku. Ačkoliv jsem letěl ve skluzu, dokázal jsem udržet zaměřovač na druhém Me 109 a zasáhnout jej. Dle mého názoru je zaměřovač K-14 v současnosti nejvýznamnějším pokrokem v bojovém vybavení."

"Me 109 měly podle všeho nějaký typ kapkovitého překrytu, měly fialové přídě a po celé délce trupu nesly hnědou kamufláž."

Nárokuji si 5 zničených Me 109." 

I přes nezvyklý průběh střetnutí (dodnes nevíme, proč první dva nepřátelští piloti vyskočili bez boje) byly všechny Yeagerovy sestřely z toho dne potvrzeny velením USAAF. Sám Yeager za svůj čin obdržel Stříbrnou hvězdu. Válku zakončil s 11,5 sestřely. Za zmínku stojí, že v březnu 1944 byl sestřelen nad Francií, strávil téměř dva měsíce v řadách francouzských partyzánů a nakonec unikl do neutrálního Španělska, odkud se v květnu 1944 vrátil zpět do Velké Británie; během přechodu Pyrenejí si navíc vysloužil Bronzovou hvězdu za to, že pomáhal jinému sestřelenému americkému pilotovi.

Po válce působil jako testovací pilot a 14. října 1947 se stal prvním člověkem, který kdy prolomil hranici rychlosti zvuku. O tom ale až jindy...

The Real. The Truth. That which eternally is.

When everything in your life feels permanent, remember this:

Some things are real—

without being permanent.

And some things remain
when everything temporary changes.

sat is one of the most profound words in Indian philosophy.

It means being.

Existence.

Reality.

Truth.

That which truly is.

We spend much of life surrounded by things that are real but changing.

Your body is real.

And changing.

Your relationships are real.

And changing.

Your career.

Possessions.

Emotions.

Opinions.

Identity.

Circumstances.

All real within experience—

and yet none remain exactly as they are.

Vedantic inquiry asks us to look deeper.

If everything I observe changes,

is there something fundamental beneath that change?

Something that does not depend upon one particular form?

This is not merely an abstract philosophical question.

It changes how tightly we hold life.

You can love something deeply while knowing its form may change.

You can participate fully without demanding permanence.

You can experience loss without concluding that reality itself has collapsed.

sat invites us to distinguish between what appears for a time—

and what ultimately grounds appearance itself.

Perhaps much of spiritual maturity is learning to give temporary things the love they deserve—

without asking them to become eternal.

One name. One truth. One step inward.

sat — the Real; that which truly is.

​Co zakázáno NENÍ:
Že spolu dva lidé chodí, žijí nebo mají intimní poměr. Žádná česká univerzita nemůže dospělým lidem zakázat soukromý partnerský život. Pokud pedagog učí na právech a studentka studuje medicínu, škola do toho nijak nezasahuje.

​Co ZAKÁZÁNO JE:
Aby vyučující svou partnerku/partnera učil, zkoušel, vedl mu práci, hodnotil ho nebo rozhodoval o jeho stipendiích.

​Jak se to řeší v praxi
​Předpisy (studijní řády, pracovní řády, etické kodexy) neříkají „rozejděte se, jinak dostanete vyhazov“.
​Ukládají pedagogovi povinnost nahlásit střet zájmů. Jakmile to nahlásí, škola situaci administrativně vyřeší:
​Zkoušení a zápočty převezme jiný kolega.
​Závěrečnou práci povede jiný vyučující.
​Vyučující nesmí zasednout ve zkušební komisi u státnic dané studentky.
​Pokud pedagog střet zájmů zatají a svou partnerku dál zkouší a hodnotí, teprve v tu chvíli porušuje pracovní i vnitřní předpisy univerzity a hrozí mu postih (od napomenutí přes odebrání předmětu až po výpověď). Vztah jako takový ale zakázán není.

477/1000 — dharmī

The one who embodies Dharma.

When you keep searching for the right thing to say, remember this:

The strongest teaching
may be the life

that no longer needs
to explain itself.

dharmī means “the one who possesses or embodies Dharma.”

There is an important progression here.

You can know a principle.

Protect it.

Practise it.

And eventually—

it begins becoming part of who you are.

At first, honesty may require effort.

You have to stop yourself.

Think.

Choose the truthful response.

Over time, honesty can become so deeply integrated that deception feels foreign.

The same can happen with generosity.

Discipline.

Patience.

Compassion.

Courage.

This is how character forms.

Repeated action gradually reduces the distance between:

“This is what I believe”

and

“This is who I am.”

Perhaps this is one reason genuinely principled people can feel different to be around.

They are not constantly performing goodness.

There is less negotiation happening inside them.

The principle has moved from rule—

to disposition.

From something remembered—

to something embodied.

To remember dharmī is to ask:

What virtue am I still performing consciously that I hope one day becomes natural to me?

The highest expression of a teaching may not be explaining it beautifully.

It may be becoming someone in whom it is visible.

One name. One truth. One step inward.

dharmī — the one who embodies Dharma.

Aseem Kumar Gupta, Additional Chief Secretary, Urban Development Department, Government of Maharashtra, was the Guest of Honour. Dr Mahendra Kalyankar, CEO, Dharavi Redevelopment Project/Slum Rehabilitation Authority (DRP/SRA), also attended the ceremony.

𝗔𝘀𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 𝗤𝟭 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟳
𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀

Think of the company as a very specialised contractor. Clients own the oilfields or the power plants. Asian Energy gets paid to do the hard, dirty, technical work on them.

It has four main shops under one roof.

𝗦𝗲𝗶𝘀𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗲𝘆𝘀. Crews send sound waves into the ground and record the echoes that bounce back. Computers turn those echoes into a map of the rock below. It is how oil companies decide where to drill without guessing. The company once owned 16,000 recording channels, and now owns 30,000. Each channel is one ear listening to the ground.

𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲. Some oilfield owners do not want to run the field day to day. Asian Energy runs it for them: the pumps, the pipes, the staff, the repairs. It is like hiring a building manager for an apartment block you own. Vedanta has handed the company a contract to manage a whole field this way.

𝗖𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴. Power plants eat coal by the trainload. Someone has to build the system that unloads it, crushes it, and carries it to the boiler. The company builds and upgrades these systems. The Mahanadi Coalfields plant at Lakhanpur is its largest coal-handling contract so far.

𝗣𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗵𝗶𝗿𝗲. This is Kuiper. Offshore rigs in the Gulf need engineers, technicians and crew. Kuiper finds them, hires them, and supplies them to energy companies. It is a placement agency whose candidates work on platforms in the middle of the sea.

The money splits into two buckets in the company's reports. In Q1 FY27, oil and gas work brought in ₹244.78 crore. Mineral and other energy work brought in ₹26.41 crore.

Most of this work comes as contracts. Contracts signed but not yet delivered are called the order book. At the June 2026 results, it was ₹1,754 crore, not counting Kuiper. About 60% of it is oil and gas work, and about 40% is mineral work.

The catch in contract work is that clients pay later. The company finishes a job, sends a bill, and waits. In FY26, the average bill took 160 days to be paid. That is more than five months for the cheque to arrive.

Shalby began in 1994 as a six-bed facility in Ahmedabad, promoted by arthroplasty specialist Dr Vikram Shah. Arthroplasty is the surgical replacement of a worn joint, usually a knee or a hip. The company now runs 13 multi-specialty healthcare facilities across 10 cities. Together they hold more than 2,200 beds. It also operates 60 outpatient centres in India and 23 clinics abroad. Those clinics sit in East African countries, Iraq, Dubai and Oman. Bangladesh and Nepal carry the rest. Few six-bed clinics attempt that curve, and fewer hospitals collect that many passport stamps.

The expansion arrived in bursts. SG Shalby opened in Ahmedabad in 2007 with 201 beds. Vapi and Krishna followed in 2012. Jabalpur, Indore and Mohali came in 2015. Jaipur, Naroda, Surat and Zynova Mumbai arrived in 2017. In the year to March 2021 the company bought Shalby Advanced Technologies, a US FDA-approved implant maker in California. It described the purchase as backward integration into orthopaedics, meaning it bought a supplier rather than a rival. A hospital group had decided it would rather make the knees than buy them.

In the three months to March 2024 came Sanar International in Gurugram, where most patient footfalls are international. Shalby paid ₹102 crore for an 87% stake in PK Healthcare, the holding company. It paid a further ₹104 crore for all of Healers Hospital Pvt Ltd. In February 2026 it subscribed to a ₹59.60 crore rights issue, an offer of new shares to existing holders. That took its stake in PK Healthcare from 87.26% to 91.13%.

China is set to lower/phase out EV export tax rebates (currently ~13% on complete NEVs), with step-down expected from around mid/July 2027. Battery VAT rebates already cut (to 0% from Jan 2027); PV rebates earlier.

This raises Chinese export costs, squeezes margins or forces higher prices, and eases pressure on competitors abroad—especially in Europe.

Likely beneficiaries:
- European OEMs: VW, Stellantis, BMW, Mercedes
- Tesla, Hyundai/Kia
- Non-Chinese battery makers (LG Energy, Samsung SDI, Panasonic)

Strongest near-term benefit is in solar (not pure EVs): Waaree Energies and Premier Energies already rallied when China cut solar/battery rebates—higher Chinese prices improve their export competitiveness.

Battery side: Higher Chinese cell costs could help Exide Industries and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility narrow the price gap as local capacity scales (though both still rely heavily on Chinese materials/cells today).

Pure auto OEMs (Tata Motors, Mahindra) see limited direct upside—Chinese passenger EV competition is restricted in India, and many still source cells from China (potential short-term cost pressure).

Policy is gradual and part of China’s broader push against overcapacity + trade friction. Not a free lunch—localization, tariffs, and demand matter more.

Not investment advice.

நீதிபதி ஜி.ஆர். சுவாமிநாதன் வழங்கிய இரண்டு தீர்ப்புகள் கவனிக்கத்தக்க முரண்பாட்டை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன.

வழக்கு 1 :- 19.12.2025-ல் தீர்ப்பளிக்கப்பட்ட Arsha Vidya Parampara Trust-ன் FCRA வழக்கு:
சம்ஸ்கிருத வேதங்கள், உபநிடங்கள், ஸ்மிருதிகள், புராணம் ஆகியவற்றைக் கற்பிக்கும் அர்ஷ வித்யா பரம்பரை என்ற மத அமைப்பு சட்டவிரோதமாக அமெரிக்காவில் இருந்து நன்கொடை பெற்றது. அதன் பின்பு FCRA license கோரி விண்ணப்பம் செய்த நிலையில், அவ்வமைப்பு "சட்டவிரோதமாக வெளிநாட்டு நன்கொடை பெற்ற மத அமைப்பு" என்ற காரணத்தின் அடிப்படையில் FCRA விண்ணப்பம் நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது. இதனை எதிர்த்து அந்நிறுவனம் உயர்நீதிமன்றத்தில் வழக்கு தாக்கல் செய்தது. இதில் தீர்ப்பளித்த, நீதிபதி சாமிநாதன் "பகவத் கீதை மத வேதம் அல்ல, அது அறநெறி நூல் மட்டுமே, எனவே அதனை கற்பிப்பது மத பரப்புரை ஆகாது" என்று கூறி அந்த அமைப்பின் விண்ணப்பத்தை, தீர்ப்பில் கூறப்பட்டுள்ள கருத்துக்களின் அடிப்படையில் பரிசீலித்து, 3 மாதங்களுக்குள் ஆணை பிறப்பிக்க வேண்டும்" என்று உத்தரவிட்டார். 

மேலும் ஒருபடி மேலே போய், அதே அறக்கட்டளையில் பெப்ரவரி 2026-ல் நடைபெற்ற நிகழ்ச்சியில் நீதிபதி சாமிநாதன் விருந்தினராகக் கலந்து கொண்டு, "பகுத்தறிவாளர்கள் ராஸ்க்கல்கள், முட்டாள்கள், காட்டுமிராண்டிகள்" என்று தனது ஆர்.எஸ்.எஸ். அமிலத்தை கொப்பளித்தார்.

அடுத்தது சமீபத்திய வழக்கு...

வழக்கு 2 :- 06.10.2026 -ல் தீர்ப்பளிக்கப்பட்ட Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust வழக்கு:
இந்தியாவில் தோன்றி இன்று ஜப்பான், சீனா போன்ற நாடுகளில் பிரபலமாக இருக்கும், பாரம்பரியமிக்க Zen தியான முறையை கற்பிக்கும் Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust-ன் FCRA license விண்ணப்பம், "மத சார்புடைய அமைப்பு" என்று கூறி விண்ணப்பம் நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது. அந்த அமைப்பும் உயர்நீதிமன்றத்தில் வழக்கு தொடுத்தது. இவ்வழக்கில் நீதியின் நிலைப்பாடு மாறுபடுகிறது. அதாவது... "FCRA விண்ணப்பம் நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது சரிதான்" என்று நீதிபதி சாமிநாதன் அடங்கிய அமர்வு தீர்ப்பளித்து விண்ணப்பதாரரின் வழக்கை தள்ளுபடி செய்கிறது. தீர்ப்பில், “Hinduism is inclusive, Abrahamic religions are inherently exclusive” என்று மத ரீதியாகப் பிரிவினையை தூண்டக்கூடிய, சமத்துவத்திற்கு ஊறு விளைவிக்கக்கூடிய பொய்யான கருத்து இடம்பெற்றுள்ளது.

இங்கே அவர் கூறும் கருத்து எழுப்பியுள்ள அடிப்படைக் கேள்வி என்னவென்றால், சம்ஸ்கிருத வேதங்கள், கீதை ஆகியவை மதத்தின் எல்லையைத் தாண்டிய தத்துவம், பண்பாடு, அறநெறி எனக் கருதப்படுமானால், ஜென் தியானம் மட்டும் ஏன் ஒரு தனி மதத்தின் அடையாளமாகக் கருதப்பட வேண்டும்? அதுவும் இந்திய கலாச்சாரத்தின் அடையாளம் தானே? இந்திய கலாச்சாரத்தை பாதுகாப்பது அரசமைப்புச்சட்டத்தின் பிரிவு 51A-ன்படி அடிப்படை கடமை அல்லவா?

ஒரு மதம் எல்லாரையும் உள்ளடக்கியது என்றும், மற்ற மதங்கள் இயல்பிலேயே பிரித்து வைப்பவை என்றும் நீதிமன்றம் கருத்து தெரிவித்திருப்பது சமத்துவம், மதச்சார்பின்மை என்ற கோட்பாட்டிற்கு எதிரானது. மேலும் அது நீதிபதிகளின் ஒருதலைபட்சமான நிலைப்பாட்டையும், சட்டத்திற்கு முன்பு சமன்பாடற்றவர்கள் என்பதையும் நிரூபிக்கும் விதமாக அமைந்துள்ளது.

Jubilant Pharmova is asking shareholders for permission to borrow up to Rs 2,500 crore, which is 29% of what it sold in the last 12 months.

THE FILING
Jubilant Pharmova's board approved issuance of up to 80,000 NCDs of face value Rs 1 lakh each, aggregating up to Rs 800 crore, via private placement in one or more tranches.
NCDs will be listed on BSE, tenure up to 5 years, coupon to be discovered via bidding.
Also seeking shareholder approval via postal ballot to issue non-convertible debt securities up to Rs 2,500 crore outstanding at any time for one year.

WHAT WE WORKED OUT (the filing does not print it)
29% of sales in the last 12 months

WHY IT IS WORTH READING
That is a large loan ask for the size of the business, and the company is asking shareholders to allow up to this much borrowing to stay on the books at any time for a year. The board has already cleared an first batch of Rs 800 crore in non-convertible debt securities (loans that do not turn into shares), with the rate to be set by bidding and a final 5 year to finish repayment window. The filing does not say what the borrowed money will be used for.

We report filings. Not advice.

BIOCON LTD - What's the story ? 

Biocon is back near its March–April lows, around the Rs 340–350 levels. Instead of looking at it as one single business, I think the simplest way to understand Biocon is to break it down into three parts:

1. Biosimilars: Developing and commercialising highly similar versions of complex biologic medicines, with growth linked to product launches, market penetration and operating leverage.

2. Generics, APIs & Formulations: Manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished medicines, where the focus is on product mix, margin improvement and sustainable growth.

3. Research, Development & Manufacturing Services: Through Syngene International, participating in the outsourced R&D, development and manufacturing opportunity for global pharmaceutical and biotech companies.

The interesting part is not just what Biocon does, but what could change over the next few years.

Some key triggers worth tracking:

1. Biosimilars scale-up :  new launches, market-share gains and broader geographic penetration.

2. Margin expansion :  better product mix, operating leverage and improved profitability. sweating of assets  and acquisitions  they did 

3. US market opportunity :  regulatory approvals, commercialisation and uptake of complex generics and biosimilars.

4. Insulin and biologics pipeline : product launches and expansion into new markets.

5. Debt reduction : deleveraging, lower finance costs and improvement in cash flows.

6. Integration benefits :  realisation of synergies across the Biocon Biologics business and a simpler operating structure.

7. Syngene growth :  recovery in client spending, new contracts and improved utilisation of research and manufacturing facilities.

8. Earnings inflection - a shift from investment-heavy growth to stronger free cash flow and sustainable earnings.

I've been following the discussion around Biocon, and @EquityValueIn has also been covering the company. Worth going through his notes to understand the business and the evolving picture in greater detail.

The reason I'm putting this out there is simple: in turnarounds, or businesses where you're betting on a change in the rate of growth, the price you pay matters a lot.

A lower entry price can provide a margin of safety, give you room to be patient and improve the risk-reward if the expected changes actually play out. It also allows time to assess whether the improvement is translating into real numbers - revenue growth, margins, cash flows and return ratios.

Of course, a stock returning to its previous lows doesn't automatically make it cheap. The thesis still needs to play out, and the balance sheet, execution and dilution risks need to be monitored.

For me, the key question is not simply whether Biocon can bounce back from Rs 340–350.

It's whether the next phase of the business can deliver a meaningful change in earnings, cash flows and return on capital  and whether the current price adequately compensates for the risks involved.

That's the part worth tracking.
