Trumpův zugzwang a Putinův gambit. 

Situační analýza

Rozruch, který vyvolala zpráva o dohodě mezi Trumpem a Putinem, spustil vlnu předpovědí: pokusí se „globální Londýn“ – využívající Zelenského jako svůj nástroj – narušit Trumpovo předvolební PR, nebo se Trumpovi podaří dostat určité ruské dodávky na trh navzdory pokračujícím úderům na ruské přístavy a ropné rafinerie?

Největším paradoxem je, že každý úder proti Rusku je koordinován USA. 
I kdyby Německo, Británie či Francie řídily údery nezávisle, operace se nevyhnutelně týkají NATO a jeho evropského velitelství. 
Vrchním velitelem spojeneckých sil v Evropě je americký generál Alex Grynkewich. 
V Evropě kolem něj neproklouzne ani moucha – natož dron či raketa. 
USA se tedy podílejí na každém evropském úderu proti Rusku a tato účast je klíčová; bez ní by takové údery nebyly možné.

▪️ Trump se momentálně nachází ve stavu zugzwang – v situaci, kdy je nutné provést tah, avšak každý možný tah vede ke zhoršení jeho pozice. 

Jaké možnosti má Bílý dům k dispozici?

1. „Nechat to vyřešit se samo.“ 
Trump ignoruje krizi cen pohonných hmot v USA a nadále manévruje na domácí scéně mezi globalisty a voliči hnutí MAGA, zatímco na mezinárodní úrovni balancuje mezi Evropou a Ruskem. 
Protahuje krize týkající se Íránu a Ukrajiny, až se nakonec stane obětí jejich společných dopadů. 
Nečinnost vede ke zhoršení Trumpovy pozice.

2. „Stůj tady – pojď sem“ (nerozhodnost / protichůdné signály). 
Trump zaujímá schizofrenní postoj: přehlíží ukrajinské údery na ruské ropné rafinerie – prováděné s pomocí Pentagonu (systémy Starlink a Palantir) – a zároveň zoufale potřebuje produkci právě těchto rafinerií, a to nejen k vítězství ve volbách, ale i k záchraně vlastního života. 
Na Trumpa se během kampaně již střílelo; pokud by čelil procesu odvolání z funkce (impeachmentu), mohl by být snadno zcela odepsán. 
Globalisté by ho buď zabili, nebo – pokud by tak neučinili – by ho nechali do konce života žít ve strachu a lekat se každého šustnutí. 
V tomto scénáři Trump ztrácí vše. 
Zelenský svou beztrestností světu ukazuje, že americký prezident je nula a že skutečný vládce sídlí v Londýně. 
Pokračující podpora Ukrajiny oslabuje Trumpovu pozici.

3. „Outsider mezi svými“ neboli „převrácení stolu“. 
Trump odstaví Zelenského a zastaví podporu Ukrajiny; má k tomu řadu možností. 
Cílem je dokázat, že zůstává dominantním alfa samcem. 
Následně je však obviněn ze zrady a potká ho stejný osud jako v prvním scénáři: oslabená pozice.

To, že se Trump obrací s žádostí o pomoc na Putina, je učebnicovým příkladem situace zugzwang. 
Nemůže si dovolit nepožádat o pomoc, avšak samotný tento krok vyostřuje jeho konflikty a staví ho do pozice slabé závislosti. 
A čím více se Trump snaží tuto dynamiku zlomit, tím silnějšímu odporu čelí – v souladu s Newtonovým zákonem: akce vyvolává stejně silnou reakci. 
Začíná rozhodování vedené emocemi namísto strategie.

▪️ Pro Putina jde o gambit: zvyšování rizika a obětování figury za účelem získání poziční výhody. 

Možné výsledky jsou:

1. „Riskoval a vyhrál“ (nejlepší možný scénář). 
Pomoc Trumpovi zvyšuje jeho šance ve volbách do Kongresu a napomáhá dosažení definitivní dohody s Čínou a Ruskem. 
Ukrajina je rozbita a rozdělena, vzniká nová bezpečnostní architektura – a to vše za situace, kdy jsou Evropě diktovány podmínky. 
Rizikem pro Rusko je, že nafta odkloněná na pomoc Trumpovi nemusí vyvinout potřebný tlak na snížení cen (300 000 tun je méně než denní spotřeba nafty v USA), a zároveň může způsobit růst cen a nedostatek paliva v samotném Rusku.

Pokud tento tah ovlivní výsledek války a podmínky poválečného míru v náš prospěch, bude gambit ospravedlněn a všichni v Rusku jej přijmou s pochopením. 
Obětujeme menší, abychom získali větší. 
Pokud se však ukáže, že Trump nic nezíská, zatímco my budeme trpět, bude nemožné tuto situaci komukoli v Rusku vysvětlit. 
Politika není kasino, kde lze prostě vsadit a přijít o peníze. 
Rusko podstupuje riziko; proto si musí od Trumpa zajistit takové podmínky, které mu zaručí prospěch již v průběhu realizace dohody, namísto čekání na konečný výsledek. 
Právě tyto záruky jsou klíčové; bez nich nemá smysl pomáhat Trumpovi na vlastní úkor.

2. „Když už nic nedoženu, alespoň se zahřeji“ (minimální cíl). 
Lze argumentovat, že Rusko těží z naplnění rozpočtu a posílení ekonomiky. 
Existuje zde i vedlejší efekt: prohloubení rozporů uvnitř NATO. 
I to je přínos, který by měl být využit, neboť ovlivní naše budoucí kroky a kapacity. 
Pokud však Trump nakonec prohraje, veškerý tento počáteční prospěch pro Rusko se nejen rozplyne, ale situace se naopak zhorší: válka se protáhne a stane se ještě brutálnější. 
Je pro Rusko zásadní právě tomuto zhoršení předejít a zajistit, aby krátkodobý zisk nezastínil možné dlouhodobé nepříznivé dopady.

3. Smíšený scénář: „Lepší vrabec v hrsti než holub na střeše“ (optimální výsledek). 
Jde o nejpravděpodobnější scénář, který kombinuje klady a zápory prvních dvou. 
Putin zahájí dodávky; Zelenský zaútočí na ruské ropné rafinerie; objem dodávek klesne; Trump zuří a váhá, ale nakonec – alespoň dočasně – odřízne Zelenského od přístupu ke službě Starlink. 
Na tuto možnost již bylo nepřímo poukázáno... ze strany Trumpa. 
Takový scénář by vedl k prudkému nárůstu ztrát v řadách Ozbrojených sil Ukrajiny (AFU), prohloubil by rozkoly kolem Zelenského a posílil vliv ukrajinské „mírové strany“ – vedené Budanovem a dalšími agenty CIA –, čímž by odsunul na vedlejší kolej „britskou frakci“ na Ukrajině a připsal jí vinu za porážku.

▪️ I kdyby „dohoda o naftě“ neměla dopad na ceny pohonných hmot v USA, Trump by přesto mohl v Šen-čenu po boku Si Ťin-pchinga a Putina dosáhnout významných výsledků a zasadit protiúder globalistům. 
Trump by z vysokých cen benzinu vinil demokraty a tvrdil, že mu zabránili v jejich snížení. 
Vyřešení tohoto vnitrounijního konfliktu by se odložilo na rok 2028, kdy by dosáhl svého vrcholu.

Aby se však tento scénář mohl uskutečnit, je klíčové, aby Rusko od Trumpa získalo nejen zmírnění sankcí a příliv deviz do rozpočtu, ale také podmínky nezbytné k odstranění evropské – a především britské – kontroly nad Ukrajinou. 
Byl by to krok k vytvoření nové bezpečnostní architektury, což je potenciální téma pro listopadová jednání v Šen-čenu mezi Putinem, Si Ťin-pchingem a Trumpem. 
Pokud by naopak u kormidla na Ukrajině zůstali britští agenti, nemělo by ani vyvolávání politických potíží pro Zelenského a jeho klan větší význam. 
Jeho nahrazení jiným londýnským chráněncem by nepřineslo žádný užitek, neboť válka by se dále vlekla a ruské náklady spojené s americkým „lend-lease“ programem dodávek nafty by přišly vniveč.

Trump je sevřen hrozbami, podobně jako štvaný vlk obklíčený řadou červených praporků. 
Pokud na ně bude jen zírat, je s ním konec; jeho jedinou záchranou je přeskočit tuto bariéru. 
Pro vlka je to děsivá představa, přesto není jiné volby – k tomuto kroku jej žene pud sebezáchovy.

▪️ Je klíčové pochopit, proč u Trumpa náhle vyvstala tak naléhavá potřeba dohody s Putinem ohledně nafty. 
Írán i Rusko čelí sankcím a provoz v Hormuzském průlivu fakticky stojí. 
Ceny v USA raketově rostou – což pro Trumpa představuje hrozbu odložené politické popravy. 
Nemá úniku; musí jednat hned.

Trh s naftou je nádrží, do níž proudí nabídka – na zdroji záleží méně než na samotném objemu; právě ten určuje ceny. 
Za běžných mírových podmínek vývozu činí podíl Ruska na tomto trhu 10–11 %. 
Válka však nyní vytvořila patovou situaci, která vede k celkovému nedostatku a růstu cen. 
Ačkoli Amerika vlastní naftu vyrábí, kdykoli ceny na zahraničních trzích převýší ty domácí, soukromí američtí dodavatelé přesměrují svou produkci na export, čímž samotné USA vystavují nedostatku a inflaci.

Právě tuto dynamiku musí Trump narušit. 
Dokáže si stát za svým? 
„Globální Londýn“ se pravděpodobně pokusí sabotovat jeho volební šance tím, že bude tlačit na Zelenského, aby útočil na ruské ropné rafinerie a přístavy – čímž fakticky zaútočí na samotného Trumpa. 
Trump má nanejvýš měsíc – možná jen tři týdny – na to, aby si před listopadem srovnal své vazaly do latě. 
Polovičatá řešení už stačit nebudou.

Splní však Trump skutečně svou hrozbu vůči Zelenskému – tedy zastavení dodávek zbraní a zpravodajských informací Ukrajině, pokud budou útoky na ruské rafinerie pokračovat? 

Ihned poté, co se objevila zpráva o dohodě mezi Trumpem a Putinem, obvinilo Zelenského nejbližší okolí Trumpa ze slabosti a zavázalo se v útocích pokračovat. 
Aby svá slova podpořili, zaútočili na ropný sklad v Azovu. 
A zaútočí znovu – o tom není pochyb – pod ochranou Londýna a Bruselu. 
Využijí k tomu ale systémy Starlink a Palantir? 
A povolí Pentagon pro tento účel využití evropských satelitů na platformách integrovaných s americkými systémy? 
Do jaké míry je navíc Trump ochoten izolovat Zelenského a riskovat konflikt s NATO ve snaze dosáhnout volebního vítězství? 
Zejména s ohledem na nepřátele, kteří proti němu stojí – nejen v Demokratické straně, ale i mezi republikány, a k tomu potenciální sabotáže ze strany Rubia a neokonzervativců? 
Je velmi pochybné, že v tom všem Trump uspěje. 
Rizika, kterým čelí, jsou zřejmá, ale jaké jsou jeho skutečné možnosti?

▪️ Trump se nyní musí stát pro Putina velmi užitečným, protože samotné ruské dodávky situaci v Americe nevyřeší. 
Podle podmínek dohody má Rusko v říjnu dodat na trh 300 000 tun a v listopadu 500 000 tun, přičemž objemy mají následně růst. 
To představuje tři supertankery o kapacitě 100 000 tun v říjnu a pět v listopadu – což není nijak závratné množství. 
Je nepravděpodobné, že by to snížilo tržní ceny, neboť ani při dodávkách do USA nelze obchodníky donutit, aby tam prodávali naftu pod tržní cenou. 
Bylo by tedy nutné zapojit Írán a zajistit souhlas Číny. 
Bez Putinovy ​​pomoci Trump taková jednání vést nemůže.
 ‼️‼️‼️‼️‼️
Trumpův zájem je jasný: potřebuje krátkodobý zásah na trhu s naftou – trvající maximálně šest měsíců – a toho nelze dosáhnout bez pomoci Ruska a Íránu. 
Co musí Trump udělat pro Írán výměnou za jeho spolupráci? 
Osobní budoucnost amerického prezidenta nyní leží v rukou Ruska, Íránu a Číny.
 ‼️‼️‼️‼️‼️
Pro Írán by mohlo být výhodné počkat, až se moci ujme Demokratická strana, a poté se pokusit vyjednat mír. 
Existuje však riziko: demokraté nemohou začít krokem, který by vypadal jako kapitulace před Íránem. 
Nejenže by se jejich preference v USA okamžitě propadly, ale Izrael a židovská lobby by jim zabránily takový krok učinit, aniž by utrpěli obrovské politické škody. 
Stručně řečeno, válka by se protahovala, což činí sázku na demokraty pro Írán riskantní. 
Bylo by lepší pokusit se uzavřít dohodu s Trumpem a zajistit si oddechový čas – výměnou za odklad sporu o Hormuzský průliv na léto a umožnění přístupu na trh s naftou (který by pak čelil tlaku zvýšené nabídky a poklesu cen). 
Čína a Rusko by však musely tato jednání usnadnit a zajistit si vlastní výhody. 
Pokud o to Trump dostatečně stojí, musí předložit konkrétní a reálné nabídky.

▪️ Výhody pro Rusko jsou v tomto případě zřejmé. 
Americké ministerstvo financí by vydalo povolení umožňující Rusku navzdory sankcím vyvážet naftu, a to s platností do dubna 2027. 
Během tohoto období by Rusko vydělalo 4,5 miliardy dolarů. 
Zelenský ani jeho evropští spojenci však nebudou nečinně přihlížet tomu, jak jim Trump kope hrob. 
Místo toho – ve spolupráci s americkou Demokratickou stranou – vykopou hrob samotnému Trumpovi.

Pro Rusko by záruky spočívaly v tom, že Washington podnikne kroky, které nejen podkopou moc Zelenského kliky na Ukrajině, ale také zlomí sevření, jímž MI6 ovládá tamní politické a mocenské elity. 

USA udělaly chybu, když řízení Zelenského zcela přenechaly Britům – situaci, kterou nyní Trump nedokáže zvládnout. 
Oslabením Zelenského pozice na Ukrajině oslabuje i pozici Londýna, tedy strany, která má na pokračování války největší zájem. 
To je ruská podmínka a to je ruská záruka.

K dosažení tohoto cíle nemusí Trump ničit City ani Bank of England. 
Stačí, když využije CIA k tomu, aby zbavil ukrajinské vedení pout, která na ně uvalila MI6 – pout, jež odsunula americké zájmy na vedlejší kolej. 

Dokud budou mít na Ukrajině hlavní slovo Britové, nemůžeme s Trumpem o této zemi konstruktivně jednat. 

Trump musí využít Pentagon k oslabení britského vojenského vlivu na Kyjev, a to s využitím dlouhodobě působící protibritské lobby mezi americkými generály. 
Britové jsou tam obzvláště nenáviděni.

Rusko se zároveň nesmí omezovat pouze na ovlivňování Trumpových zájmů a přitom ignorovat hluboce zakořeněné vazby jeho rivalů. 

Vždy Rusko sázelo na osobní kontakty se zahraničními lídry v domnění, že prokazování osobních laskavostí z nich spolehlivě učiní ruské spojence. 

Tato taktika však všude selhala. 

Jak v Evropě, tak v SNS nepřinesly osobní vazby dlouhodobý zahraničněpolitický úspěch. 

Příkladem mohou být Schröder, Berlusconi, Kočarjan, Sargsjan, Alijev, Janukovyč či Sarkozy... 
Tito lídři čelili odporu a opustili úřad, aniž by Rusku zanechali jakýkoli vliv. 
Stojí za to opakovat tuto taktiku u Trumpa?

Tento přístup obvykle předpokládá, že Rusko uzavře dohodu s nejvyšším představitelem, který pak vše správně zařídí – což implikuje, že dotyčný nemá žádné střety zájmů a disponuje absolutní mocí. 
Tak to ale nefunguje. 
Každý lídr je výsledkem kompromisu mezi elitami a tento kompromis je formován silami, které jsou mimo kontrolu jak nás, tak našich „partnerů“.

▪️ V každém případě musí Rusko rozbít sítě a kanály vlivu, které využívají ruští společní protivníci. 
Pokud toho ruští partneři nejsou schopni nebo to odmítají udělat, nemohou Rusku poskytnout to, co potřebuje. 
Stejně tak by neměli dostat to, o co žádají. 
Trump by od Ruska neměl dostávat dary v naději na budoucí vděčnost. 
Každý tanker s naftou, který Rusko dodá, by měl přinést nejen tvrdou měnu a omezení vojenské pomoci Ukrajině, ale také oslabení britské pozice v této zemi.

Pouze takové podmínky představují adekvátní dohodu. 
Rusko nemůže dodávat naftu Trumpovi – zatímco je pod útokem evropských raket a dronů naváděných Pentagonem – z Kyjeva ovládaného Brity. 

Stejně tak nemůže podporovat Trumpa za cenu posilování britského agenta Zelenského. 
Zelenský není ani tak dvojitým agentem sloužícím CIA a MI6; patří jednoznačně Britům. 
Rusko nemá žádný užitek z Trumpa, který zde není schopen nic změnit. 
Musí pochopit, že ve vztahu k Putinovi nemůže sedět na všech židlích najednou. 
A je klíčové, aby mu to Rusko – zdvořile, avšak důrazně – vysvětlilo hned na začátku.

Žádné výsledky ve válce – tedy pouze údery na rafinerie a přístavy spolu s dodávkami zbraní a zpravodajských informací – znamenají, že žádný další tanker nebude. 
Takové jsou podmínky férové ​​dohody. 
Rusko nespolupracuje s nikým za nerovných podmínek. 
A na tomto postoji trvá; o něm se nediskutuje.

Ramkrishna Forgings–Titagarh: Understanding the Rail Wheel JV

Apart from Titagarh’s core railway operations , there is the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels JV, between Ramkrishna Forgings (51%) and Titagarh Rail Systems (49%).

The JV was formed to manufacture forged railway wheels, primarily for Indian Railways, and is building a large manufacturing facility in Chennai.

The key points to understand:

1. The JV has a 20-year contract with Indian Railways for around 15.4 lakh wheels, with an assured requirement of roughly 80,000 wheels per year.

2. The plant is being developed with a much larger installed capacity of ~2.28 lakh wheels per year.

3. This is important: 80,000 wheels is the contracted offtake, while 2.28 lakh is the potential manufacturing capacity. The balance capacity will need to be filled through additional domestic and export customers.

4. Total project cost is around ₹2,000 crore, with equity already being infused and the plant progressing toward commercial production.

5. Trial production/commissioning activity has started, with commercial production targeted around FY27.

6. Management has indicated an initial FY27 production target of roughly 45,000–50,000 wheels, with production potentially increasing to around 1 lakh wheels in FY28 and eventually reaching the full 2.28 lakh capacity.

7. At full capacity, management has indicated potential revenue of roughly Rs 2,500–2,800 crore annually. This is a capacity potential, not a confirmed revenue forecast.

8. The real opportunity is therefore bigger than the Indian Railways contract.

If the JV can successfully qualify the product and ramp production, the additional capacity can potentially be sold to:

- Indian Railways & Other domestic railway customers
- Titagarh's own requirements
- European  & North American customers
- Other export markets

This is where the second leg of the story comes in. The Indian Railways contract provides an anchor customer and initial demand visibility, while the larger 2.28 lakh-wheel capacity creates the possibility of building a much larger domestic + export business.

For Titagarh, there is also a strategic benefit from vertical integration. Wheels are an important input for wagons and passenger coaches, so having access to a dedicated wheel manufacturing business can improve supply security and potentially support its broader rail manufacturing operations.

For Ramkrishna Forgings, the JV provides entry into a large and specialised railway-component opportunity and potentially creates a new export-oriented business alongside its existing forging operations.

The opportunity is large, but the important part is still ahead: converting installed capacity into actual demand and profitable production.

Swan Defence Set to Win ₹1,897 Crore Tanker Order — First Locally Built Oil Tankers in 25 Years, Beats Cochin Shipyard with $48.9 Million per Vessel Bid for Four Dual-Fuel MR Tankers

Core Theme 
Swan Defence’s win of the ₹1,897 crore MR tanker order, edging out Cochin Shipyard on price, marks the first tangible test of India’s state-backed push to revive domestic shipbuilding, reviving oil tanker construction after 25 years and adding to a growing order book of ammonia carriers, chemical tankers and green tugs

The Order
Mumbai-listed Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Ltd (SDHI) is set to win a ₹1,897 crore (~$196 million) order from a proposed joint venture of state-run shipping and oil marketing companies led by Shipping Corporation of India (SCI)

Covers construction of four dual-fuel ready Medium Range (MR) product tankers, the first such carriers to be built locally in 25 years

SDHI, which has a technical tie-up with Samsung Heavy Industries Co. of South Korea, quoted about $48.9 million per vessel when price bids were opened on Friday (October 9), multiple sources said

SCI floated a tender for two firm and two optional dual-fuel ready MR tankers, each able to load 17,000-18,000 tons of cargo

The Competition
SDHI pipped state-run Cochin Shipyard Ltd, which quoted about $4 million more per vessel

The order, once signed, will boost the order book of SDHI, India’s largest shipyard by dry dock capacity

The yard re-started operations in 2024 under a new management led by Swan Corp

Existing Order Book
Energy ONE Ltd: four dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers, worth $240-280 million (₹2,230-₹2,603 crore)

European shipowner Rederiet Stensen AS: six chemical tankers of 18,000-ton capacity, each worth $227 million

Svitzer Group A/S (Copenhagen-based towage and marine services specialist): contract for four biofuel-powered TRAnsverse tugs, worth about ₹500 crore

The yard is led by Vivek Merchant

Policy Context
This is the first attempt in a quarter of a century to build oil tankers locally

It kicks off a much-awaited government plan to scale up the shipbuilding industry with order support from state-run firms, on the back of the ₹69,725 crore package approved by the Cabinet in September 2025

👉 Why does this matter?
  → Semiconductors require precision equipment and tightly controlled components.
  → Aerospace & defence demand specialised manufacturing and rigorous quality control.
  → EVs need precision gears, shafts, motor components and driveline systems.
  → HVAC depends on compressors, bearings and reliable rotating machinery.
  → Industrial automation needs accurate tooling, motion-control systems and repeatable manufacturing processes.

👉 Moving from assembling finished products to developing the underlying engineering capabilities, tooling, manufacturing processes and critical components.
👉 Manufacturing creates products. Precision engineering builds the capability to manufacture them consistently, competitively and at scale.

AI boom fuels scramble for data centre capacity ( Mint Article)

Data centre capacity pre-leased by companies more than doubled in just a year

Yadukrishna CS & Jas Bardia

📍 Mumbai/Bengaluru

Hyperscalers and large companies are increasingly booking data centre capacity before facilities are ready, with pre-leased capacity more than doubling in a year as demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure outpaces new supply.

Pre-leased data centre capacity rose to around 1.2 gigawatts (GW) as of June 2026, from around 550 megawatts (MW) a year earlier, according to data published in a 23 August report by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield. The capacity refers to the amount of computing infrastructure a data centre can support, measured by the power available to run IT equipment.

Pre-leasing, or early booking of under-construction data centres, is an established practice worldwide. In India, for example, Adani Enterprises Ltd, one of the country’s largest industrial conglomerates, has bet on 1GW of cumulative data centre capacity, anchored by hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft and Google.

The rush to secure capacity reflects the growing demand for AI and cloud infrastructure in India. Companies are committing earlier because data centres take time to build, with land, power connectivity, approvals and construction all adding to the time needed to bring new capacity online.

“Supply of data centre capacity takes more time because large data centres require land, power connectivity, approvals and significant construction periods,” said Vinish Bawa, a partner at consultancy PwC India. “This is encouraging customers to commit to capacity earlier rather than wait for facilities to become operational,” he added.

The rise in data centre utilization has made India “Asia's fastest-growing data centre market, driven by hyperscale investments, AI workloads, and transformative tax incentives,” according to a 31 August note by real estate consultancy Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) India. The Indian government is offering a tax holiday until 2047 for foreign cloud service providers that use Indian data centre infrastructure.

India's data centre capacity stood at 1.7GW as of June 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield, and is expected to reach 5.6GW by 2030 at a 33% annualized growth rate.

While pre-leased capacity has doubled, vacancies at operational data centres have also fallen to very low levels, underscoring strong demand for existing capacity. Only 2.8% of the country’s operational data centres remained vacant, according to Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) India.

Further, 100MW of information technology (IT) capacity was sold to cloud-service clients between January and June 2026, while 84.9MW was operationalized during the same period.

Demand is being driven by rising smartphone use and consumer AI applications such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini. In February, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said ChatGPT had over 100 million weekly active users in the country, underlining the need for local data storage and processing capabilities.

“Record-low vacancy rates and massive pre-commitments are creating enterprise supply constraints while attracting unprecedented foreign capital for self-build facilities. Sustainability initiatives, robust policy frameworks, and renewable energy expansion are cementing India's role as a strategic global leader in AI-ready infrastructure," according to a note by Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) India.

The model puts paid-for comfort where permanent buildings are difficult, and folds it away when the season turns.

The hospitality arm builds what the presentation calls asset-light, non-permanent, ultra-premium glamping structures. Glamping is camping with hotel fittings, hotel service and a hotel bill. The stated logic is that lightweight, design-led rooms can go where permanent construction is difficult. Tent City Narmada carries 200 tents across 1,24,000 sqm. White Rann has 76 rooms. Bangaram in Lakshadweep has 45 cacoon-shaped rooms and five shell-shaped rooms. Praveg Caves at Jawai has 12 cave-style rooms. Disclosed average prices start at ₹2,995 at Damanganga Resort in Silvassa. They reach ₹25,715 at Bangaram, inside the same brand.

The second engine is events and exhibitions. The work includes state assemblies, summits, governmental pavilions and temporary legislative facilities. The presentation claims more than 1,000 events delivered and more than 2,000 exhibitions managed. Management addressed this line on the November 2025 call. It said the business once ran at ₹50 to 80 crore, before 2020-21. That fell to about ₹10 crore. Management said a new team and a newly appointed CEO are rebuilding it. It also said resorts had taken priority for roughly one and a half to two years.

The third engine is advertising, through Abhik and Bidhan. The portfolio holds 800 private hoardings across Ahmedabad, Baroda and Rajkot. It holds exclusive rights to more than 800 HPCL hoardings across Gujarat and Rajasthan. Government advertising runs in UFO digital theatres. The company also holds exclusive rights to operate 120 smart toilets in Ahmedabad under a PPP model. Forty are installed, and the advertising rights run for 15 years. The same company sells sunrise over the Rann and wall space in a municipal toilet.

The spending follows the building. Depreciation for the year to March 2026 was ₹48.80 crore. Finance costs were ₹14.49 crore. Management described the lease commitments owed to the government as fixed. The company sold 1,21,700 rooms in the year to March 2026. The prior year figure was 88,426. Lending lifecycle solutions cover loan origination, loan management, collections, fraud detection and tools using generative artificial intelligence. PSB Xchange is a digital marketplace connecting public sector banks, corporates and smaller businesses.

The architecture is pitched as a single shared chassis. Management describes it as "not building multiple products in parallel…all of these products on the same chassis." The company was incorporated in August 1990 as IT&T Enterprises Private Limited. CARE Ratings, a credit-rating agency, records that it began in business process outsourcing, which is clerical work done under contract for other firms. Three and a half decades later it designs missile subsystems, radar electronics and aerospace parts. Few founding documents survive a journey of that length.

The present shape came from acquisitions. CARE's note records that successive mergers turned the outsourcing firm into an engineering design services business. Its customers sat in aerospace, defence, heavy engineering and automobiles, along with industrial products. CARE records that further acquisitions took it into defence system integration, covering hardware and product design, development and deployment. The consolidated group runs to sixteen entities on CARE's list. They include an American Inc., a UK Limited, a German GmbH and a Canadian company. A design company in Wuxi is on the list as well. The annexure reads more like a frequent-flyer statement than a subsidiary schedule.

The current chapter starts in the three months to December 2024. CARE records that Dr. Sampath Ravinarayanan returned then as Chairman and Managing Director. He launched the Power 930 programme, targeting ₹9,000 crore of revenue by March 2030. The same programme targets ₹960 crore of profit after tax by that date.

The method is a portfolio inversion. CARE records management's view that engineering services is highly competitive, with limited long-term growth. CARE also records management's position that the company already holds foundational capabilities in manufacturing. Those cover aerospace, defence and the ESAI vertical. So the services businesses go and manufacturing comes in. CARE puts the planned greenfield and inorganic spend at over ₹2,200 crore. The divestment brings in about ₹2,256 crore. The two figures are close enough to rhyme.

The paperwork has moved quickly through the year. The board approved the transfer of the heavy engineering, automotive and energy services businesses on 26 May 2026. It approved the aerospace services transfer on 12 June 2026. Shareholders approved both on 27 July. On the buying side, the company announced a 90% acquisition of Cloud Wave Technologies for about ₹234 crore, completed on 10 September 2026. The board approved a non-convertible debenture issue of up to ₹200 crore on 5 September to fund it. Debentures of that kind are borrowings that never turn into shares. The 36th annual general meeting is set for 28 September 2026.

• إحنا عندنا حالتين لنادي الزمالك، والحالتين خاصين بشيكوبانزا، والحالات دي اتكررت كتير في الدوري المصري، ويمكن اتكررت في أول أسبوع في ماتش الأهلي والشرقية إنتي

• في الحالة الأولى على مروان عطية، بعد ما الكورة اتصدت وردت، الكورة راحت على الجنب، وبعد كده حصلت عرضية، وفيه إيد موجودة من مروان في ظهر شيكو

• السؤال هنا: هل الإيد دي دفعت؟ وهل عملت حاجة؟ لأن في حالات زي دي، اللاعب بيرتكز على لعبة واحدة وبيحاول يطلع ياخد الكورة، وبعدين بيتعرض لدفعة، حتى لو بسيطة، بتخليه يختل توازنه بالشكل ده وما يعرفش يطلع يقابل الكورة وهي نازلة

• الدفع اللي بنتكلم عليه دايمًا هو: هل الدفع مؤثر ولا غير مؤثر؟ الدفع هنا ضعيف، لكنه مؤثر في اللعبة، ودي ركلة جزاء لم تُحتسب لنادي الزمالك

• كان المفترض على حكم تقنية الفيديو إنه يستدعي حكم الملعب ويوريه إن فيه دفع، لأن الإيد هنا مش موجودة من غير تأثير، لكن فيه دفع بسيط، والحالة دي اتكررت أكتر من مرة

• فيه دفع بسيط، لكنه مؤثر، وبيخرج اللاعب اللي بيحاول ينط علشان يلعب الكورة برأسه من اللعبة، وبالتالي دي ركلة جزاء غير محتسبة

• اللعبة دي اتكررت مرتين، علشان محدش يقول إننا بنتكلم عن الأهلي والزمالك بس

• اتكررت في ماتش الأهلي والشرقية في أول أسبوع، في لقطة بن شرقي، واتكررت مع محمد شحاتة، واتقال وقتها برضه إنها ركلة جزاء غير محتسبة لنادي الزمالك 

• لجنة الحكام قالت إن دي ركلة جزاء غير محتسبة، وبالتالي الدفع البسيط المؤثر لازم تكون ليه عقوبة، ودي ركلة جزاء غير محتسبة لنادي الزمالك

• بالنسبة للحالة التانية لشيكو بانزا مع اشرف داري، لازم نفرق بين اتجاه الكورة في الحالة دي واتجاهها في الحالة الأولى

• لو الكورة جاية من ناحية المدافع، فالمدافع هو الأقرب ليها، لكن لو الكورة جاية من ناحية المهاجم، فالمهاجم بيحاول يحجز على كورته، وده حقه

• التحجيز عندنا نوعين: الأول إن اللاعب يتوقع الكورة هتنزل فين، ويبدأ يتحرك على الأساس ده وياخد المدافع في ضهره، والنوع التاني إن الكورة تكون على الأرض واللاعب يحجز عليها

• من حق اللاعب إنه ياخد مكانه والكورة في الهوا، ويقف ويستنى لحد ما تنزل علشان يلعبها

• الكورة في الحالة دي جاية من ناحية المهاجم، وبالتالي المفترض إنها تكون أقرب ليه

• شيكو بانزا كان سابق الكورة وعايز يقف علشان الكورة تنزل قدامه، وبدأ يحصل الاحتكاك

• لو الاحتكاك تم بالجسم، والمدافع عينه على الكورة، فده ممكن يكون طبيعي، لكن هنا المدافع بدأ يستخدم إيده علشان يمنع شيكو بانزا من الوقوف

• في كل الفريمات اللي عرضناها، الإيد فضلت موجودة، والدفع استمر مرة واتنين وتلاتة، رغم إن الكورة كانت بتقرب من مكان شيكو

• ممكن حد يقول إن المهاجم هو اللي واقف ومانع المدافع أشرف داري من الوصول للكورة، لكن المدافع كان يقدر ينط ويلعب الكورة، وده شيء بنشوفه كتير

• المفروض إن المدافع يروح للكورة ويظهر للحكم إنه بيتنافس عليها، لكن لو كل هدفه إنه يمنع المهاجم من الوقوف على رجليه، فده مختلف عن التنافس على الكورة

• في آخر لقطة، الكورة نزلت فعلًا في المكان اللي كان واقف فيه شيكو بانزا وخبطت فيه، وده معناه إن الكورة كانت نازلة في المكان اللي المهاجم كان موجود فيه لاعب الزمالك 

• أنا مش بلعب اسكواش؛ مش معنى إن لاعب واقف قدامي وبيحاول يلعب الكورة إني أقف في ضهره وأقول إنه منعني من الوصول ليها

• هنا المفروض إنك تنافس على الكورة، مش تنافس المنافس نفسه، ولو كنت بتنافس على الكورة مكنش هيبقى عليك مخالفة

• بالتالي، ركلة الجزاء التانية غير محتسبة لنادي الزمالك

• ووفقًا للتحليل، الزمالك كان يستحق ركلتي جزاء في الحالتين أمام الأهلي

Titagarh Rail Systems Ltd was, until a name change, Titagarh Wagons Limited. The new name reads like a company noting politely that it has other interests now. It was incorporated in 1997. Crisil, a credit-rating agency, records that it was established in July 1997 by Mr Jagdish Prasad Chowdhary, with operations managed by Mr Umesh Chowdhary. It makes freight wagons, passenger coaches, metro trains and train electricals. It also makes steel castings, specialised equipment, bridges and ships, for domestic and export markets.

Crisil records four Indian manufacturing plants: two in Titagarh, one in Uttarpara in West Bengal and one in Bharatpur, Rajasthan. Between them they can make 12,000 wagons and 300 coaches a year. Casting steel capacity is around 30,000 tonnes a year. The investor presentation adds engineering centres in Hyderabad, Bangalore and Kolkata. It also lists regional offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai, and depots in Pune, Surat and Ahmedabad. A firm that began by welding steel boxes now runs a depot network.

The last two years have been a sustained exercise in corporate rearrangement. The shipbuilding and maritime business went to wholly owned subsidiary Titagarh Naval Systems Limited for ₹114.88 crore. That transfer took effect on 1 January 2026 and was disclosed in February 2026. It has been reported as discontinued operations since. The entire shareholding in Titagarh Singapore Pte Ltd was sold for USD 154,707. The share purchase agreement was executed on 27 March 2026, and the entity ceased to be a subsidiary from 5 May 2026.

The Italian associate, Trasporti Ferroviari S.p.A, was formerly Titagarh Firema S.p.A. It sold its business unit to Fabbrica Italiana Treni for 66,095,000 euros in March 2026. The board approved a full exit on 31 May 2026. The notes record that Firema was admitted to liquidation proceedings on 23 July 2026.

Meanwhile the joint ventures multiplied. Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels is a tie-up with Ramkrishna Forgings, and there is a propulsion venture with ABB. A consortium with BHEL covers Vande Bharat sleeper trains. A fifty-fifty joint venture is proposed for maintaining 80 trainsets over thirty-five years. The org chart now requires its own org chart. Four plants, three engineering centres and three depots sit under one listed company.

**The main legal issues raised in the post (and its immediate thread) are these:**

- **Lanham Act § 43(a) reverse passing off for creative works**  
  The post’s core discussion is accurate: after *Dastar Corp. v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corp.* (2003), reverse-passing-off claims under the Lanham Act are heavily restricted when the dispute involves writings, analyses, videos, frameworks, or other communicative/expressive content. The Supreme Court held that “origin of goods” means the producer of the tangible product offered for sale, not the author of the ideas or content embodied in it. Allowing reverse-passing-off claims merely to force authorship credit would create a perpetual quasi-copyright outside the Copyright Act’s limited term and formalities. Courts (including in Oregon) have applied this to reject pure attribution claims for copyrightable or copyrighted expressive material. Lack of credit alone is generally not enough when the defendant produces the copies being distributed.

- **Copyright as the primary available remedy**  
  The post correctly identifies copyright infringement (unauthorized reproduction, distribution, or derivative works of original expression fixed in a tangible medium) as the stronger and more direct route for the types of Blogspot writings, behavioral analyses, frameworks, and videos the author describes. It notes the practical advantages of U.S. Copyright Office registration (statutory damages, attorney’s fees, presumptions of validity, and the ability to sue in federal court) and the utility of DMCA notices. Ideas, facts, and concepts themselves are not protected—only the particular expression.

- **Narrower surviving Lanham Act theories**  
  False-advertising claims under § 43(a)(1)(B) can sometimes still be viable if a defendant makes affirmative, material commercial misrepresentations about the nature, characteristics, qualities, or source of the work (beyond simple non-attribution). Reverse passing off remains more available for tangible physical goods from which marks are removed. State unfair-competition claims are generally weak alternatives for pure creative works because they often track *Dastar* and face copyright preemption under 17 U.S.C. § 301 when they essentially allege unauthorized copying of expressive content.

- **Personal allegations of trademark theft and related harms**  
  The author claims she has a “stolen trademark,” has been deemed too disabled to own her own agency or work, and is on fixed income. In the surrounding thread she alleges long-running appropriation of her research/blog content (described as reverse passing off and related cybersquatting), identity issues, and inaction by Eugene Police on reports she says she mapped out. These remain unadjudicated public assertions; the post itself frames the legal discussion as general information, not legal advice for any specific situation, and notes that outcomes depend on facts, evidence, and jurisdiction.

- **Police / institutional response issues**  
  Hashtags and related posts in the thread allege that police have engaged in or enabled reverse passing off, treated crime victims as enemies, or failed to act on mapped reports involving IP and related claims. Police generally have broad discretion not to investigate civil intellectual-property disputes; such matters are ordinarily pursued through civil litigation, Copyright Office processes, or platform tools rather than criminal enforcement.

In short, the post’s doctrinal summary of *Dastar* and the limited role of reverse passing off for creative works is solid, while the personal trademark, disability, content-appropriation, and police-related claims are presented as the author’s own unresolved allegations. For any real dispute of this type, copyright registration and enforcement plus consultation with an IP attorney are the pathways the post itself emphasizes.

#TimeTechnoplast #TIMETECHNO #CorporateGovernance #Subsidiaries

Part 3: Closing out the series with the corporate structure and governance side — five subsidiaries/corporate actions, plus the guidance track record and ownership table that didn't make the first two posts.

TPL Plastech (74.86%-owned, FY26 revenue ₹422.7 Cr) is being absorbed into the parent — we flagged the swap ratio as unannounced in Part 1, and it's since been confirmed: 403 Time Technoplast shares per 1,000 TPL Plastech shares, ~79.02 lakh new shares, roughly 1.6% dilution, effective 1-Apr-2026. 

The Middle East 50% stake sale (~30% of overseas revenue, ~USD 25mn indicative value, JPMorgan/EY advising) is still open with no binding agreement. A new ₹50 Cr investment for 65% of Time Intercontinental Ltd — a promoter-promoted entity for raw-material sourcing — sits below the related-party materiality bar but is worth tracking. 

Power Build Batteries (97.04%-owned, the Energy Storage arm covered in Part 2) absorbed NED Energy in 2025. And the proposed Ebullient Packaging acquisition, guided "firm" for March 2026, was dropped in August citing Middle East cost volatility.

On who's actually buying this: Industrial Packaging serves 900+ institutional customers across 11 countries — mostly chemical and process-industry buyers who specifically demand recognised brands, which is a real pricing-power moat since the company competes with only Schutz and Mauser globally in IBCs. 

Composite Cylinders sells LPG cylinders to PSU oil marketing companies (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL — 20+ lakh supplied to IOCL alone) and CNG cascades across 22 City Gas Distribution entities. 

PE Pipes goes to EPC contractors executing government schemes (Nal Se Jal, Smart City Mission, Swachh Bharat). 

MOX Films/Technical Products supplies auto OEMs — Ashok Leyland, Tata Motors, Volvo — plus 450+ dealers for the Techpaulin consumer brand. 

Worth flagging: the highest-margin composite segment leans heavily on PSU demand, and the company has previously seen tender delays tied to PSU leadership transitions.

On governance: MD and CFO roles are combined in one person, a structure that's been stable for years; board refresh in August was routine, not a pressure exit; promoter pay sits at 21.1x median employee pay, nothing unusual; auditors gave an unqualified FY26 opinion with no Section 143(12) fraud flag; CRISIL rates the company AA-/Stable and A1+.

The part worth sitting with is the guidance scorecard: of 9 tracked commitments since Q3 FY25, only 2 were met or are on track, 2 were outright missed (the debt-free timeline, and Ebullient), and 5 landed partial or below range. That's a moderate record, not a strong one — worth discounting future guidance by 10-15% until delivery improves. Promoter holding has fallen from 51.62% to 47.56% since the Nov-25 QIP, with DII ownership rising to fill the gap.

Dne 11. října 1797, během bouřlivého období Francouzských revolučních válek, došlo k rozhodujícímu střetnutí na moři u Camperdownu. Zde se britské Královské námořnictvo, pod energickým velením admirála Adama Duncana, utkalo s Královským nizozemským námořnictvem, které vedl viceadmirál Jan de Winter.

Tato bitva představovala klíčový a největší konflikt mezi námořními silami Velké Británie a Nizozemí v rámci této války. Following up on the funnel post below: here's what's actually being built, where, and how big each segment can get.

1. Industrial Packaging runs on scale, not fresh capacity — 11 countries, 20+ India plants, ~1,80,000 tonnes of polymer processed a year, 55%+ of the domestic market. The constraint here is customer pricing-formula renewal, not physical capacity, and FY27E revenue is guided to grow at a steady 12% (₹3,819 Cr → ₹4,277 Cr).

2. Composite Cylinders is where the capex is actually going. The new Morai, Gujarat plant takes CNG cascade capacity to 1,080 units, and this segment is guided to grow 27% (₹2,286 Cr → ₹2,903 Cr) — more than double the packaging growth rate, and at 17-18% EBITDA margins versus 12-13% for legacy packaging.

3. PE Pipes picked up a bolt-on in June: 76% of Systoverse Pvt Ltd (₹25 Cr) for a branded, ISI-certified sprinkler/pipe business in Maharashtra at a concessional 15% tax rate. Order book sits at ~₹235-260 Cr, management guides 20-25% segment growth, and the business is seasonally back-loaded — historically ~35:65 H1:H2.

4. Energy Storage (97.04%-owned Power Build Batteries) is the smaller, specialised bet — OPzS tubular batteries for utilities and e-rickshaw batteries for India's ~16 lakh e-rickshaw fleet, run-rate ~₹125 Cr, targeted to grow ~30% YoY for three years with margins improving from ~12% toward 15%. MOX Films and technical products round out the portfolio as a small, stable, no-major-capex niche.

5. The headline number for FY27: total capex guided at ₹350 Cr, which management itself frames as a "consolidation year" rather than a fresh expansion cycle — most of that capital is going toward the composite-cylinder ramp.

‘Indian Pharma’s Risk Aversion Holding Back Innovation’: Biocon’s Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw — Calls for Digital Technology to Speed Up Drug Development as Industry Leaders Push for a Shift Beyond Generics

Core Theme 
Indian pharma’s leaders agree that the sector’s generics-heavy, risk-averse model, which captures about 20% of global value despite its volume share, must give way to a continuous innovation pipeline, with Mazumdar-Shaw urging digital tools and regulatory alignment to speed development while Sun Pharma’s $11.75 billion Organon deal and licensing-led scale-building show how companies are trying to move up the value chain.

The Core Argument
Indian pharmaceutical industry’s aversion to taking risks poses a major hurdle for innovation and needs to change with the use of technology, says Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, chairperson, Biocon

“In pharma and biopharma, the pipeline is the lifeline”

She stressed the need to replenish the drug development pipeline continuously

Said at a meeting on quality management in New Delhi last week

Event: a two-day programme organised by the Indian Foundation of Quality Management, a consortium of companies including Tata Sons, TVS Motors, Biocon, Sun Pharma, Boeing and Motherson

Panel included Dilip Shanghvi (Exec Chairman, Sun Pharma) and Glenn Saldanha (Chairman, Glenmark Pharma); the three leaders discussed the sector’s future direction and India’s shift from a long history of generic drugs toward innovative medicines

Drug Discovery Is Risky
Drug discovery is fraught with risks, with only one or two out of 10 candidates advancing to the final stages and meeting commercial milestones

Biocon has advanced an anti-cancer drug to Phase III clinical trials

She noted that India’s regulatory progress is gaining momentum

On aligning with regulators: “We made slow progress... and now it looks positive”

Time to leapfrog with the help of digital technology; India should deep dive and emulate not just China but also countries like Australia to move molecules rapidly into the clinic and beyond

Mazumdar-Shaw said most Indian companies, at home and abroad, are yet to make this shift, and that this needs to change

Shanghvi: Innovation as Priority
Dilip Shanghvi (Sun Pharma): focus on innovation should be the priority if the company wants to grow and help patients

Sun Pharma has agreed to buy US-based Organon for a record $11.75 billion earlier this year

Said generic drugs account for a large share of global pharmaceutical sales by volume but only 20% by value

“If we want to succeed and become big globally and help patients, our focus on innovation is needed”; this also ties with PM Narendra Modi’s objective of Viksit Bharat by 2047

Organon deal could help Sun Pharma launch innovative products globally

In Europe, China, Korea, Taiwan, Australia, Turkey and other countries, Sun lost time registering products, and in countries like Brazil and Mexico, it did not have the infrastructure; Organon gives it the ability and a higher share of innovative drugs

Organon also gives Sun the familiarity needed to manage faster licensing; “we need a continuous pipeline” and should see a lot in the next five to 10 years

Saldanha: Three Categories and Scale
Glenn Saldanha (Glenmark): “We need a continuous pipeline, and we should see a lot in the next five to 10 years”

Indian pharma companies broadly fall into three categories: generics, generics and biosimilars, and innovation-led businesses

Building scale in innovation through deals or licensing is important

बाद में बचा हुआ 114 Drums Oil गुजरात से तमिलनाडु भेजा गया।

📌 Department ने देखा कि Truck में 114 Drums थे, जबकि E-Way Bill में 110 Drums दिखाए गए थे।

1/2 🗳️⚠️ Naše Česko získalo prvního senátora zvoleného pod svou značkou, ale Tomáš Fiala je dlouholetý místní politik, který mandát pouze obhájil.

⁉️👤 Kdo je „první senátor“ hnutí Naše Česko? 

Tomáš Fiala, 69letý pediatr a dlouholetý ředitel Nemocnice Strakonice. Narodil se ve Strakonicích, v tamní nemocnici pracuje od roku 1983 a od roku 2003 ji řídí.

🗳️👤 Fiala nevyhrál pouze ve městě Strakonice. Obvod č. 12 zahrnuje celý okres Strakonice a západní části Písecka a Prachaticka, tedy také Písek, Vimperk, Vodňany, Blatnou či Volyni. Je to výrazně regionální mandát.

🗳️ Výsledek byl mimořádně přesvědčivý: Fiala dostal 55,41% a 24 643 hlasů, takže mandát obhájil už v prvním kole.

Ještě výraznější je srovnání s rokem 2020. Tehdy Fiala jako nestraník za ODS získal v prvním kole jen 27,84% a ve druhém porazil lidovce Luboše Peterku těsně 8 238 ku 8 193 hlasům – rozdílem pouhých 45 hlasů.

Tentokrát však kandidovali jen tři lidé, zatímco před šesti lety jich bylo jedenáct.

⚠️🚧⚠️ Fialových 55% proto nelze mechanicky vykládat jako zdvojnásobení podpory Našeho Česka. Nabídka byla mnohem užší a hlasy se méně tříštily.

ℹ️ Senátní volby jsou silně personalizované. Volič často nevybírá ideologii či celostátní program, ale známého lékaře, starostu, hejtmana nebo ředitele instituce, kterému připisuje konkrétní výsledky.

⚠️👤 Fiala je přesně tento typ kandidáta. Jeho politickým kapitálem není především značka Naše Česko, ale dlouhé spojení s regionem, nemocnicí a zdravotnictvím. V Senátu navíc vedl zdravotnický výbor a působil v klubu ODS a TOP 09.

⚠️🚧⚠️ Naše Česko nevytvořilo vítězného kandidáta od nuly. 

Převzalo zavedeného senátora, který byl v roce 2020 zvolen s podporou ODS, měl šest let na budování mandátu a disponoval vlastní profesní i regionální značkou.

Fiala se ke Kubovi přidal prakticky okamžitě po jeho odchodu z ODS na konci listopadu 2025. Důležitý detail: sám Fiala členem ODS nikdy nebyl, v roce 2020 kandidoval jako nestraník. Z ODS tedy formálně neodešel, změnil však politickou podporu a už 3. prosince 2025 oznámil, že mandát bude obhajovat za tehdy ještě nepojmenované Kubovo uskupení. 

V senátorském klubu ODS a TOP 09 přitom zůstal až do konce volebního období.

Jejich spojenectví nevzniklo ze dne na den. Kuba jako hejtman a Fiala coby ředitel krajské Nemocnice Strakonice dlouhodobě spolupracovali při správě zdravotnictví, investicích i během pandemie. 

Fiala své rozhodnutí zdůvodnil tím, že v novém hnutí vidí nejlepší cestu k podpoře regionu a výkonu senátorské práce. Nešlo o náhodně získaného kandidáta, ale o člověka z Kubova dlouhodobého jihočeského profesního a mocenského okruhu.

⚠️🚧⚠️ Přesto jde pro Martina Kubu o důležitý úspěch. 

Poprvé se ukázalo, že kandidát může opustit značku ODS, kandidovat pod Naším Českem a svou podporu nejen neztratit, ale výrazně mobilizovat už v prvním kole.

Výsledek tak testoval hlavně přenositelnost důvěry: od osobnosti k nové značce a od bývalé jihočeské ODS ke Kubovu hnutí.

⁉️🗳️👤⚠️ V tomto omezeném regionálním testu přenos fungoval. Nevíme však, kolik lidí volilo Naše Česko a kolik jednoduše „svého doktora Fialu“.

⚠️🚧⚠️ Je také nepřesné tvrdit, že Naše Česko „získalo prvního člověka v Senátu“. Už před volbami se k němu hlásili senátoři Fiala a Zbyněk Sýkora.

Nové je to, že Fiala byl nyní poprvé přímo zvolen na kandidátce Našeho Česka.
Pro poměr sil v Senátu proto nejde o nový mandát navíc, ale o obhájené křeslo pod novou značkou.

Politická hodnota je hlavně symbolická a organizační: Naše Česko už není jen projekt založený přeběhlými regionálními politiky, ale značka potvrzená voliči.

⚠️🗳️⚠️ Ještě důležitější zprávou pro Kubu jsou komunální volby v Českých Budějovicích. 

Naše Česko tam získalo 29,18% a 15 mandátů, zatímco ODS spadla z 29,35% v roce 2022 na 7,57%. To už není jen osobní Fialův příběh.

⚠️🚧⚠️ Budějovický výsledek naznačuje, že Kuba dokázal převést podstatnou část někdejšího jihočeského elektorátu ODS na vlastní značku.

#TimeTechnoplast #TIMETECHNO #PlasticProducts #IndustrialPackaging

Time Technoplast has spent three decades replacing metal with plastic — and the business model is literally a funnel: each layer funds the one above it.

1. Industrial Packaging is the cash engine — world's largest plastic-drum maker, #3 globally in Intermediate Bulk Containers, 55%+ of the domestic Indian market, ₹3,819 Cr of FY26 revenue (62.6% of the total). That cash funds Composite Cylinders, the growth-and-margin engine: world's #2 maker of Type-IV composite cylinders, ₹2,286 Cr FY26 revenue, running 17-18% EBITDA margins versus 12-13% for legacy packaging. And that, in turn, funds the newer, smaller bets — PE Pipes (order book ~₹235-260 Cr), Energy Storage (~₹125 Cr run-rate) and MOX Films/technical products.

2. The growth catalysts sit mostly in the middle layer: India has ~50 crore LPG cylinders in circulation on a 15-year replacement cycle — roughly 3 crore cylinders a year of addressable demand, with 20+ lakh composite cylinders already supplied to IOCL alone. CNG cascades serve 8,000+ stations, and a new Gujarat greenfield plant lifts cascade capacity to 1,080 units. There's a genuine optionality leg too — Time Technoplast is the first in India with PESO approval for Type-IV hydrogen storage cylinders, an early bet on the hydrogen economy. PE Pipes rides government infra schemes (Nal Se Jal, Smart City Mission) plus a fresh FY26 gas-distribution licence.

3. Worth being honest about the watch items, not just the story: FY26 free cash flow actually turned negative (-₹137 Cr) on inventory hedging and working-capital build, partially reversing in Q1 FY27. The "debt-free" framing nets off ₹342 Cr of unutilised QIP cash sitting in FDs — gross balance-sheet debt is still ~₹639 Cr. Update on the TPL Plastech merger: the swap ratio is now announced (board decision 29-Sep) — 403 Time Technoplast shares for every 1,000 TPL Plastech shares, ~79.02 lakh new shares to be issued, works out to roughly 1.6% dilution on the current share base. That's modest — this one's resolved, and smaller than it looked while open guidance credibility is moderate — only 2 of 9 tracked guidance items were met or beaten, and the Ebullient Packaging acquisition was guided firm, then reversed.

A genuinely interesting, self-funding business model — just one where the growth catalysts and the watch items both deserve equal airtime.

​วรรณกรรมส่วนใหญ่มันยังมีจังหวะให้ตัวละครได้ลุกขึ้นสู้ หรืออย่างน้อยก็ได้หยุดพักหายใจ แต่เรื่องนี้เหมือนกับการเดินลงเหวที่ลึกลงเรื่อยๆ โดยหาทางออกไม่เจอ

​ทุกหน้าเต็มไปด้วยความอ้างว้างและความล้มเหลวในการอยู่ร่วมกับคนอื่น เนื้อหาหม่นมาก แตะทั้งเรื่องซึมเศร้า การทำร้ายตัวเอง และการจากไปด้วยตัวเอง ใครที่ใจไม่ค่อยไหวอยู่แล้วควรระวังก่อนเปิดอ่าน (ส่วนตัวผมไม่แนะนำในช่วงที่จิตใจอ่อนแอ)

​ผมอ่านแล้ววางไม่ลง... แต่ก็อ่านต่อไม่ไหวแล้วเหมือนกัน เลยค้างอยู่กับความรู้สึกนี้มาหลายวันแล้ว

Eight weeks of pain finally ended. Nifty snapped its longest losing streak in 25 years. But crude oil, FII selling, and an RBI rate hike made sure the recovery was fragile.

Here is everything that moved the Indian market this week (October 5–9, 2026). Save it, share it, bookmark it.

WEEKLY SCORECARD

Sensex: 72,472 (up 0.8%)
Nifty: 22,520 (up 0.4%)
Bank Nifty: 55,256 (down 1.5%)
MidCap: Up 1.6%
SmallCap: Up 0.5%
India VIX: Elevated

The Nifty snapped its eight-week losing streak — the longest in 25 years. But the weekly gain was barely 0.4%. That tells you the recovery is weak.

DAY BY DAY BREAKDOWN

- Monday: Green start. Nifty crossed 22,500. Softer crude and better breadth gave some breathing room.
- Tuesday: Nifty touched 22,776 — the high point of the week. Two straight days of gains raised hopes of a real reversal.
- Wednesday: Everything changed. RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shifted to calibrated tightening. Selling returned immediately.
- Thursday: The bloodbath. Nifty crashed to a fresh 52-week low of 22,179. Crude oil above $100, US bond yields near 5.3%, rupee at 96.78, and relentless FII selling. This was the worst day of the week.
- Friday: The bounce. Sensex surged 879 points to 72,472. Nifty jumped 289 points to 22,520. IT and FMCG led the rally. TCS reported strong Q2 earnings.

Net result? A week of two halves. The first three days looked like a recovery. The last two days were pure panic. Friday saved the week from being a ninth straight loss.

WHO MADE MONEY THIS WEEK

- Trent +13.1% (Q2 operational update showed healthy Westside and Zudio sales growth)
- BSE +7.9%
- PNB +6.8%
- Kotak Mahindra Bank +5.4%
- Vedanta +4.7%
- TCS +3.8% on Friday (Q2 profit up 14.9% YoY to ₹13,884 crore; AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, now over 10% of total revenue)
- ITC +4.3%
- Eicher Motors +4.2%
- Apollo Hospitals +4.7%

The Nifty IT index was the best-performing sector, gaining 3% on Friday alone. FMCG rose 2.2%. PSU Bank gained 1.6%.

WHO GOT HURT

- Avenue Supermarts (DMart) -7.8% (muted store expansion and rich valuations overshadowed 18.4% YoY sales growth)
- Vedanta Aluminium Metal -7.7%
- Jindal Steel -7.6%
- Siemens Energy -7%
- Adani Enterprises -6.5%
- Max Healthcare, Hindalco, Bharat Electronics were among the biggest losers on Nifty.
- BSE fell 2% on Friday despite being a weekly gainer. Reliance Industries slipped 0.45%. JSW Steel edged down 0.15%.

SECTOR PERFORMANCE

Green zones: IT (+3%), FMCG (+2.2%), PSU Bank (+1.6%), Private Bank (+1.4%), Auto (+1.4%), Media (+1.2%), Metals (+1.1%)

Red zones: Oil and Gas (the only sector in the red on Friday)

Mixed: Realty, Consumer Durables advanced modestly. Financial services gained 1.7% for the week.

The real story is the RBI rate hike. Fourteen of 16 major sectoral indices ended lower on Wednesday after the rate hike. Auto fell 1.6%. Realty dropped 1.8%. Metal declined 2.3%. FMCG fell 0.9%.
But by Friday, most sectors recovered. The IT rally saved the day.

THE BIG DRAMA: RBI HIKES RATES BY 25 BPS

The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening. This was the first rate hike since February 2023.

Why? Crude oil above $100, a weakening rupee, and persistent inflation concerns. The RBI felt it had no choice.

The impact was immediate. Auto stocks fell as higher interest rates threaten vehicle financing. M&M fell 1.9%. Maruti dropped 1.5%. Ashok Leyland crashed 2.9%. Realty stocks got hammered — DLF fell 1.5%, Godrej Properties dropped 1.8%, Prestige Estates plunged 2.6%. Metal stocks bled — Hindalco fell 2.7%, JSW Steel lost 2.4%.

But banking stocks recovered from initial losses after the policy announcement. Kotak Mahindra Bank and PNB actually gained during the policy day rebound.
The message is clear: the RBI is worried about inflation. Rate cuts are off the table.

WHAT OUTSIDE INDIA DID TO US

- Crude Oil: Brent stayed above $100 all week. The US-Iran conflict remained unresolved. Any escalation and crude spikes higher. Every dollar above $100 hurts India wider trade deficit, weaker rupee, higher inflation.
- US Bond Yields: The 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5.3%. High US yields pull money out of emerging markets. That is exactly what happened to India.
- FII Selling: Foreign investors sold ₹30,294 crore this week. FIIs were net sellers in all five trading sessions. Thursday alone saw ₹12,944 crore of selling — the largest single-day outflow of October so far.
- DII Buying: Domestic institutions bought ₹30,313 crore this week. DIIs provided consistent support. Their strongest buying of ₹10,703 crore also came on Thursday. They offset over 80% of FII selling on that day.
- The Tug-of-War: FIIs sold ₹30,294 crore. DIIs bought ₹30,313 crore. The net flow was positive by just ₹19 crore. That is how close this fight is.
- Rupee: The rupee closed at 96.78 against the dollar. It stayed weak all week but strengthened slightly on Friday. The RBI intervened to prevent sharp falls.

IPO MARKET WAS ACTIVE

- Jio Platforms IPO: The price band has been set at ₹1,065–1,119 per share. The IPO is expected to open on October 21 and list on October 28. Issue size is about ₹37,700 crore at a valuation above ₹12 lakh crore. This could be India's biggest IPO ever.
- Fusion CX: Price band set at ₹275–289 per share. Issue opens October 14, closes October 16. The company is an AI-powered customer experience solutions provider. Revenue grew 37% to ₹1,818 crore in FY26. Net profit more than doubled to ₹170 crore.
- HD Fire Protect: IPO opens October 13. Price band details awaited. Listing expected October 21.
- Swara Baby Products: FirstCry-backed company received SEBI approval to raise ₹1,000 crore.
- Zetwerk: Plans up to $525 million India IPO next week.
- Carlsberg India, TMC Transformers, Ujin Pharma, Matangi Rubber received SEBI approval for IPOs.

The pipeline is massive. Liquidity is being diverted toward these IPOs, which is limiting the broader market recovery.

COMPANY NEWS THAT MOVED STOCKS

- TCS: Reported Q2 net profit of ₹13,884 crore, up 14.9% year-on-year. Annualized AI-related revenue reached $3.1 billion, crossing 10% of total revenue for the first time. The company also said the US suspension of firms from the Permanent Labor Certification Program was not expected to materially affect its workforce strategy. Stock surged 3.8% on Friday.
- SEPC: Signed a ₹854.57 crore infrastructure contract with SAIL for the Pellet Plant BOP package at the SAIL-IISCO Steel Plant in Burnpur. Order book now exceeds ₹10,000 crore. Stock gained 7.1%.
- Power Grid: Commissioned its 2,500 MW solar transmission project in Bidar, Karnataka. Commercial operations began October 5. Stock rose 1.1%.
- Titan: Fell 4.1% on Wednesday after weaker-than-expected jewellery growth in the September quarter.

- Hexaware: Announced a multi-year tie-up with Anthropic.
- KEC International: Bagged fresh orders worth ₹1,030 crore.
- Air India and Air India Express: Hiked fuel surcharge on domestic and international flights from October 9.
- TCS: Kept lower outlay for quarterly variable pay in Q2 amid margin pressure.
- Goldman Sachs: Bought 0.5% stake in JTL Industries, sold 0.59% in AceVector.

HIDDEN GEMS

- Trent surged 13.1% after its Q2 operational update showed healthy growth in sales led by new Westside and Zudio store additions. Delivery volumes were 1.2X the previous month. This is a genuine consumer story.
- BSE gained 7.9% for the week despite falling 2% on Friday. India's exchange business is booming.
- PSU Banks are showing relative resilience. PNB gained 6.8%. The Nifty PSU Bank index rose 1.6% on Friday.
- ARCIL hit a 10% upper circuit. Kanohar Electricals rallied 20% to hit a 52-week high after Q1 results.

The real money is often where nobody is looking.

ECONOMIC SIGNALS

- RBI Rate Hike: The repo rate is now 5.50%. The stance is calibrated tightening. This is a clear signal that the RBI prioritises inflation control over growth support.
- Rupee at 96.78: The currency stayed weak all week. A weak rupee is good for IT exporters but bad for importers. The RBI is walking a tightrope.
- Crude above $100: This is the single biggest risk to the Indian economy right now. It widens the trade deficit, pressures the rupee, and keeps inflation high.
- Q2 Earnings Season: TCS kicked it off with strong numbers. More results coming next week. Analysts expect Q2 earnings to be softer than Q1. This is why the market is fragile.
- Manufacturing PMI: Was at a seven-month high of 55.1 in September. The economy is strong. The market is just scared.

TECHNICAL LEVELS FOR MONDAY

- Nifty support at 22,200–22,180. A decisive break below this range could accelerate the decline toward the psychological 22,000 mark.
- Nifty resistance at 22,500–22,600. A sustained move above 22,600 could open the way for a recovery toward 22,800.
- Nifty is currently at 22,520. The index formed a Doji candlestick on the weekly chart, indicating indecision between buyers and sellers.
- Bank Nifty support at 54,500. Current level is 55,256.
- India VIX remains elevated. Fear is not gone — it is just resting.
- The 200-week EMA near 22,382 is an important technical level. The weekly close was marginally above it.

- How did US markets close on Friday? US yields are still near 5.3%.

- Rupee movement. If it weakens past 97, expect more FII selling.

- FMCG stocks like ITC, HUL are defensive plays in uncertain times.

- Trent is on a run. Q2 operational update was strong.

EVENTS TO WATCH

- Q2 Earnings Season: Infosys, HCL Tech, Wipro, and other IT majors report next week.
- Jio Platforms IPO: Price band set. Issue opens October 21.
- Fusion CX IPO: Opens October 14.
- HD Fire Protect IPO: Opens October 13.
- US inflation data: Will decide the Fed's next move.
- US-Iran negotiations: Any breakthrough could cool crude oil.

OCTOBER WARNING

- October is historically a volatile month for global markets. The 1987 crash, the 2008 Lehman collapse, and the 1929 crash all happened in October.
- The key risks are crude oil direction, US bond yields, and FII selling. If the 10-year stays above 5.3%, FIIs will keep selling.
- Nifty snapped its eight-week losing streak, but the recovery is fragile. Friday's bounce was driven by TCS earnings and short covering. Do not FOMO into it.

MORAL OF THE WEEK

- Eight weeks of losses finally ended. But the weekly gain was just 0.4%. That is not a recovery — it is a pause.
- The RBI hiked rates. FIIs sold ₹30,294 crore. Crude stayed above $100. The rupee stayed weak. And yet, the market finished green. That tells you DII buying is powerful.
- Friday's rally was real. TCS delivered strong numbers. IT stocks led the bounce. But the Nifty still finished below Tuesday's high of 22,776. So the week ended with a rebound, not yet with proof of a reversal.
- The economy is strong. Manufacturing PMI is at a seven-month high. GDP growth is 7.8%. But the market is scared of crude, the RBI, and FII selling.

When the market is confused, cash is your best friend. Keep some dry powder ready. The bounce, when it comes, will be sharp. You want to be ready for it.

Irdai Seeks Commission Caps Implementation by April — Reforms May Start January 1, Insurance Distribution Stocks Sell Off as PB Fintech Tumbles 36%

Core Theme 
Irdai is pressing ahead with a cost-cutting overhaul of insurance distribution, capping commissions and tightening expense limits to make cover cheaper and push growth into smaller towns, even as the proposals have wiped out value in distribution stocks and drawn job-loss warnings from brokers; with a January or April start on the table and consultations still open, the final shape of the caps remains the key unknown for banks, insurers and fintech platforms.

Timeline and Intent
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) may implement sweeping distribution reforms from January, pushing ahead with an overhaul that has battered shares of insurers and brokers

Effective dates under consideration: January 1 and April 1, said Girija Subramanian, whole time member (distribution), in an interview

A January start underscores the regulator’s determination to reshape the economics of selling insurance, after concluding that an earlier liberalisation failed to improve cost discipline

The Proposals
Last month Irdai proposed capping commissions paid by insurers to brokers and other distributors, to lower fees for consumers and encourage more people to take out insurance

Caps would apply to most forms of insurance

Regulator also plans to enforce lower management expenses over time to help bring down costs

Reductions would be phased in over five years, with the first interim milestone in the financial year ending March 2029

Market Fallout
Proposals triggered a sharp selloff in companies exposed to insurance distribution

PB Fintech (parent of Policybazaar) tumbled 36% when the moves were announced

Turtlemint Fintech Solutions has plunged by half since then

Measures could slash fee income for banks and digital brokers by as much as 90% in high-margin categories, according to analysts

Risks are higher for fintech platforms; the proposed 10% cut in new business commission rates translates to a 10%-12% fall in their earnings, according to Jefferies Financial Group Inc.

Job-Loss Fears and Regulator’s Response
Insurance Brokers Association of India warned changes could affect as many as 1 million jobs

Subramanian rejected concerns of large-scale job losses, saying the reforms should instead generate employment by widening the distribution network and making it easier for new participants to enter

Brokers are in talks with the regulator as they seek changes to the proposals

Why Irdai Is Acting
Commissions have grown faster than premiums since rules were relaxed in 2023, while higher distribution spending hasn’t produced a corresponding expansion in insurance coverage

Expenses at private life insurers climbed to about 22% of total premiums, from 16% in FY21

For private general insurers, expenses rose to roughly 32% from 25% in FY19

Rewards paid to distributors have in some cases added 30% to 60% to base commissions

Rural Expansion Incentives
Proposals include incentives for distributors to expand beyond major cities

Business from towns with populations of fewer than 1 million could earn an additional 10% of the applicable commission limit, rising to 20% for areas with fewer than 50,000

Consultation Process
Insurers, brokers and other stakeholders have until October 25 to submit comments on the consultation paper

Irdai will examine suggestions before issuing draft regulations; these will then be opened for another round of public feedback before the final framework is issued

Volby do Knesetu 27. října: jak se hlavní strany staví k palestinskému státu, Západnímu břehu a Gaze? Přehled podle izraelských médií.

Palestinský stát dnes neprosazuje žádná ze sionistických stran. Liší se v tom, co se Západním břehem: anektovat ho, držet pod bezpečnostní kontrolou, nebo se od Palestinců oddělit. V Gaze se přou o to, zda pokračovat podle Trumpova plánu, nejdřív vojensky porazit Hamás, nebo pásmo obsadit a osídlit.

VLÁDNÍ BLOK

Likud (Netanjahu)
• Palestinský stát: dokud bude Netanjahu premiérem, nevznikne v Gaze ani na Západním břehu
• Západní břeh: na dotazy médií strana neodpověděla
• Gaza: armáda se nestáhne, dokud Hamás nebude skutečně odzbrojen

Ocma jehudit (Ben Gvir)
• Palestinská samospráva: odzbrojit a zbavit majetku
• Západní břeh: plná suverenita, nové osady, legalizace všech předsunutých osad
• Gaza: „dobrovolná emigrace“, žádná dohoda s Hamásem

Náboženský sionismus (Smotrich)
• Palestinský stát: osidlování ho má fakticky znemožnit
• Západní břeh: plná suverenita, cíl milion židovských obyvatel
• Gaza: dobýt zbytek pásma a založit židovské osady

Šas a Sjednocený judaismus Tóry
• Vlastní plán nemají. Šas je proti palestinskému státu a podporuje pravicové iniciativy

Amcha Jisra'el (Winter)
• Palestinský stát: nikdy
• Západní břeh: suverenita
• Gaza: rozhodné vítězství a „dobrovolná emigrace“

OPOZICE

Jašar! (Eizenkot)
• Palestinský stát: není na stole; výhledově „autonomie bez armády“
• Západní břeh: proti anexi; schválené osady v oblasti C ponechat, nelegální předsunuté osady v oblastech A a B vyklidit
• Gaza: Trumpův plán, ale nejdřív úplné odzbrojení Hamásu

Bejachad (Bennett, Lapid)
• Palestinský stát: jednoznačně proti
• Západní břeh: oblast C jako budoucí izraelské území
• Gaza: Egypt místo Turecka a Kataru, volná ruka pro izraelskou armádu

Jisra'el bejtenu (Lieberman)
• Palestinská samospráva: rozpustit, dohody z Osla zrušit
• Západní břeh: suverenita v oblasti C; v oblastech A a B má běžný život spravovat Jordánsko
• Gaza: zlikvidovat Hamás, pak předat správu vnějšímu aktérovi

Demokraté (jediná levicová strana, Golan)
• Palestinský stát: konečnou podobu nechává otevřenou, od autonomie po dva státy
• Západní břeh: proti anexi, pro oddělení od Palestinců; vyklidit nelegální předsunuté osady
• Gaza: Trumpův plán a palestinská vláda technokratů

ARABSKÉ STRANY

Společná kandidátka (Džabarín)
• Palestinský stát, konec okupace, vyklizení všech osad, okamžité ukončení války v Gaze

Ra'am (Abbás)
• Dva státy na základě dohody, proti anexi

Ani opozice není jednotná: Eizenkot chce palestinskou samosprávu zachovat, Lieberman rozpustit. Bennett s Liebermanem mluví o suverenitě v oblasti C, Eizenkot s Golanem jsou proti.

Zdroje: odpovědi stran pro ynet, rozhovory v Times of Israel a N12, Israel Hayom.

Pozn.: Kvůli srozumitelnosti pro českého čtenáře používám místo korektního označení Judea a Samaří v zahraničí běžnější název Západní břeh.

Sammaan Capital Q1 FY 27 

Key Financial & Operational Figures

Assets Under Management (AUM): Stood at INR 56,239 crores (with overall earning power assets at ~INR 53,000 crores).

Disbursements: INR 3,875 crores in Q1 (~INR 3,900 crores referenced across 12,000 new customers).

Product Breakup: INR 664 crores for home loans, INR 2,000 crores for loans against property (LAP), INR 840 crores in a credit fund deal (20% retained), INR 100 crores in unsecured/portfolio buyouts, and INR 262 crores in loans against securities.

Profit After Tax (PAT): INR 243 crores for the quarter.

Asset Quality & Capital: Capital Adequacy ratio is comfortable at 20.1%. Net NPA stands standard at 0.15%. Gross recoveries were INR 424 crores (Net recoveries at INR 240 crores).

Disbursement Targets: Target of INR 30,000 crores for the current financial year (H1: INR 10,000 cr, H2: INR 20,000 cr) and INR 40,000 to 50,000 crores for the next financial year.

🏆 The Four Pillars of Strategy

The management is focusing its multi-decade growth strategy on four core pillars:

1. Liability Franchise & Credit Ratings
Upgrades: Domestic ratings upgraded from AA to AA+, and international ratings from B+ to BB-. The company plans to target AAA domestic rating by financial year 2028.

Cost of Funds: Has dropped by 90 basis points from 10.5% to 10%. Management expects it to drop to 9.3% by the end of the year and reach the 7%-8% range over 2–3 years.

Completed a $63 million buyback of dollar bonds to strengthen market confidence.

2. Asset Growth & Product Expansion
Transitioning from a monoline mortgage lender into a multi-product platform.

Moving from purely secured lending (currently 97% of AUM) to a target mix of 80% secured and 20% unsecured next year.

Actively expanding the physical footprint from 240 branches to a target of 800 branches by the end of next year via a hub-and-spoke model.

3. Technology Landscape & AI Adoption

Building a completely fresh, "digital-first" tech stack without legacy burdens.

Launching an updated customer app alongside Salesforce CRM and a new loan management system in H2 FY27.

Implementing 53 AI use cases, with 60% expected to go live within the financial year, primarily focused on risk, compliance, and cross-selling.

4. Governance & Assurance

Integrated IHC nominees onto the board, including Mr. Alwyn Crasta (Group CFO) and H.E. Dalia Khorshid.
In the final stages of selecting a new statutory auditor from the top five audit firms.

Concluding a partnership with a top-five firm to co-source and reinforce the internal audit function this quarter.

🔍 Key Analyst Q&A Highlights

Pricing Strategy: On being asked about pricing competitiveness, management stated they will leverage a mix of balance-sheet holdings and securitisation. They plan to consistently securitise 30% of what they originate to maintain an asset-light framework.

Cost-to-Income: Cost-to-income is projected to hover around 50% this year due to aggressive expansion opex, but is expected to decline to 30%–35% by FY29 as operating leverage kicks in.

IHC Benefits: Tangible benefits include immediate annualized savings of INR 450 crores (potentially scaling to INR 1,000 crores) due to lower funding spreads, alongside 30%–50% cost reductions in software vendor procurement due to IHC's corporate scale.

IHC’s Vision for India: H.E. Dalia Khorshid emphasized that IHC views Sammaan Capital as a growth platform. While currently focusing on stabilizing and scaling digital lending, they plan to eventually evaluate broader fintech, asset management, and financial ecosystem opportunities.

🚨 PB FINTECH: NOMURA SLASHES TARGET BY 31%, CUTS FY28 PROFIT ESTIMATE BY 72%!

Policybazaar parent PB Fintech gained around 2.5% to ₹1,020.50 on October 9, even as Nomura sharply reduced its valuation following proposed insurance commission reforms.

NOMURA'S BIG DOWNGRADE IN ESTIMATES 📉

🔹 Rating: Neutral, unchanged
🔹 New target price: ₹1,100
🔹 Previous target: ₹1,590
🔹 Target reduction: ~31%
🔹 FY28 profit estimate cut: 72%
🔹 FY29 profit estimate cut: 51%
🔹 FY28 insurance premium estimate cut: 13%
🔹 FY29 insurance premium estimate cut: 19%

WHY SUCH A SHARP CUT? ⚠️

IRDAI's proposed insurance distribution reforms could significantly reduce commissions earned by intermediaries.

Nomura's revised model assumes:

🔹 PB Fintech exits the POSP business
🔹 Lower insurance distribution take rates
🔹 FY28 expenses reduced by 40%
🔹 FY29 expenses reduced by 48%
🔹 Policybazaar, Dubai and corporate business assumptions remain unchanged

PROFITABILITY UNDER PRESSURE 📊

Nomura now forecasts:

🔹 FY28 EBITDA margin: 7.9%
🔹 FY29 EBITDA margin: 18.2%
🔹 Long-term revenue CAGR assumption: 13.2%, down from 15.1%

The brokerage also outlined two alternative scenarios:

🔹 ₹1,335 fair value if health insurance commission caps increase by 2 percentage points
🔹 ₹1,366 fair value if Policybazaar successfully expands into traditional savings insurance products

These are hypothetical brokerage scenarios, not guaranteed outcomes.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The biggest concern isn't simply slower premium growth. It is the possibility that lower commission rates could fundamentally change PB Fintech's profitability.

Even after assuming substantial cost reductions, Nomura has cut its FY28 profit forecast by 72%.

That highlights how sensitive the insurance distribution business is to regulatory changes.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

IRDAI's final regulations, commission caps, POSP business restructuring, cost reductions and new revenue streams will determine the company's earnings outlook.

Importantly, the regulations are still proposals. The final framework could differ materially from the consultation paper.
